entries.title: Interactive Bicycle Explainer: Gemini vs GPT-6.2 Astra
entries.description: Comparison of Gemini 4 Carbon and GPT-6.2 Astra building an interactive HTML webpage explaining bicycle parts from a photo, including the full reusable prompt used for the task.
entries.prompt:
请把这张自行车照片做成一个面向新手的交互讲解网页,交付完整、可直接在浏览器打开的单文件 HTML。CSS 和 JavaScript 全部内嵌,不依赖外部库或联网资源。

要求:
1. 保留原照片作为主要展示区域,不要用另一辆自行车或示意图替换。照片应内嵌在 HTML 中;如果当前环境无法读取或内嵌附件,请明确说明限制,不要假装已经完成。
2. 在照片中你能清楚辨认的 6–10 个真实部件上放置可点击标记,不足 6 个时宁缺毋滥。标记必须指向对应部件,缩放或切换到手机屏幕时也不能错位。
3. 点击标记后,高亮对应位置,展示部件名称、用一句通俗中文解释的用途,以及这张照片中可直接观察到的特征。支持关闭说明、切换部件。
4. 严格区分"照片观察"和"一般知识"。遮挡、模糊或看不到的部分标为无法判断,不要补画隐藏部件,不要猜测品牌型号、价格、车架材质或变速档数。
5. 页面简洁,中文显示正常,电脑和手机都能使用。提供与标记对应的部件列表,让用户也能通过列表选择部件。
6. 不提供拆卸、维修或安全状态判断。

完成后,请交付 HTML 文件(如环境不支持附件,则输出完整代码),并简短列出:识别了哪些部件、哪些信息无法从照片确定、是否有未实现的要求。不要用功能描述代替实际可用的成品。
entries.translated_prompt:
Please turn this bicycle photo into an interactive explanatory webpage for beginners, delivering a complete, single-file HTML that can be opened directly in a browser. All CSS and JavaScript must be embedded inline, without relying on external libraries or network resources.

Requirements:
1. Keep the original photo as the main display area; do not replace it with another bicycle or diagram. The photo should be embedded in the HTML; if the current environment cannot read or embed attachments, clearly state the limitation and do not pretend to have completed it.
2. Place clickable markers on 6-10 real parts that you can clearly identify in the photo; prioritize quality over quantity if fewer than 6 are visible. Markers must point to the corresponding parts and remain aligned even when scaling or switching to mobile screens.
3. When a marker is clicked, highlight the corresponding location, display the part name, explain its purpose in simple colloquial Chinese, and describe observable features from this specific photo. Support closing explanations and switching between parts.
4. Strictly distinguish between "photo observations" and "general knowledge." Mark obscured, blurry, or invisible parts as "undeterminable," do not draw hidden parts, and do not guess brand/model, price, frame material, or gear count.
5. Keep the page clean, ensure Chinese displays correctly, and make it usable on both desktop and mobile. Provide a list of parts corresponding to the markers so users can also select parts via the list.
6. Do not provide disassembly, repair, or safety status judgments.

Upon completion, deliver the HTML file (or output the complete code if attachments are not supported), and briefly list: which parts were identified, which information could not be determined from the photo, and whether there are any unfulfilled requirements. Do not substitute functional descriptions for actually usable finished products.

entries.title: Fidget Toy Design Challenge
entries.description: Prompt for designing a working fidget toy in Blender with mechanical constraints (gears, no glue).
entries.prompt:
I gave GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, and Gemini 4 Argon the same challenge: design a working fidget toy in Blender that I could 3D print, assemble, and test.
At least three mechanically coupled gears, fully printed parts, and no glue, metal screws, or purchased bearings. Then I tested the actual prints to see how the designs held up.
Astra had the smoothest movement. Opus made the most satisfying-looking design. But Gemini combined a more intricate mechanism with the most comfortable grip, so it takes the win for me.
Which one would you pick? #gpt6astra #opus55 #gemini4argon #3dprinting #3ddesing

entries.title: Single Prompt Mario Kart Game Build
entries.description: Benchmarking artistic quality by building a Mario Kart-style racing game using a single prompt with AI coding tools.
entries.prompt:
There are two important points:
・For better or worse, this is about as far as you can get with a single prompt.
・Conversely, you can also look at it this way: you can get this far with just a single prompt.

For the purpose of benchmarking artistic quality, I built a Mario Kart-style racing game using GPT Codex and Claude Code with a single prompt.
The person controlling this game is the account owner, Backer.
Although the gameplay video only shows a portion of the game, I built an entire stage without omitting any parts, from the title screen through the main loop to the end-condition check.

-----
â– Left
-----
Claude Code Opus 5.5 | Amount of thinking:Ultracode
Claude Code Sonnet 5.5 | Amount of thinking:Ultracode

Point:
・Only the Claude Code was used.
・Claude work time: 6 hours 35 minutes
・API time included: 7 hours 20 minutes
・Backer himself did not write any code this time.
・Blender, MCP, Godot, Unity, Unreal Engine, etc. were not used.
・Professionals, amateurs, and beginners alike can all game operate and create game system content in the same way.

-----
â– Center
-----
GPT-6 Astra Codex | Amount of thinking:Ultra

Point:
・Only the Codex was used.
・Codex work time: 68 minutes
・Backer himself did not write any code this time.
・Blender, MCP, Godot, Unity, Unreal Engine, etc. were not used.
・Professionals, amateurs, and beginners alike can all game operate and create game system content in the same way.

-----
â– Right
-----
GPT-6 Astra Codex | Amount of thinking:Extremely high

Point:
・Only the Codex was used.
・Codex work time: 47 minutes
・Backer himself did not write any code this time.
・Blender, MCP, Godot, Unity, Unreal Engine, etc. were not used.
・Professionals, amateurs, and beginners alike can all game operate and create game system content in the same way.

-----
â– Important
-----
On social media, you often see videos claiming that "AI created a complete Mario Kart with just one prompt," but that's a lie.
If it was truly created using only CodeAI (such as Codex or Claude Code) and no external tools, then it's only natural that it would "look like this," for better or for worse.
For a game to be polished, it's essential for the developers to fine-tune every element, including the program, system (game loop, game status management, character status management, state flag bits, event flag bits, proper variable definitions, structure/class management, pointers, pointer lists, functions, function lists, interrupt handling, hit detection, coordinate calculations, camera coordinates, lighting adjustments, shadow mapping, improving processing speed in real space, screen space, and projection space, etc.), modeling, shading, UI, sprites, creation and adjustment of various effects, presentation adjustments, coordinate movement, fading, alpha ring blending, sound production, and sound effect production.

-----
â– Supplement
-----
On social media, you often see accounts trying to gain impressions or lying, posting things like, "The gaming industry is over! This was done with just one click and one line of prompts!" along with videos of existing, finished commercial games.
Frankly, these fake posts benefit no one and are not funny at all. Replies like, "This post isn't even funny as a joke," are common to these kinds of posts.
Instead of making such pointless posts that only waste viewers' time, it's far more worthwhile to look at the insights of people who bravely share the progress of their own games, even at the risk of their ideas being stolen, or, like Backer's posts, who complete a full stage and post it as an integrated benchmark (artistic benchmark).
At the very least, it's far better than looking at countless unfunny, fake posts that post things like, "The gaming industry is over! This was done with just one click and one line of prompts!" along with videos of existing, finished commercial games.

Developer:
Backer | AAA programmer who has been active from the GBA era to the present.
I developed 2D and 3D games using C and C++ even before the days of the Engine.
Formerly CAPCOM Third Development Division (Console Game Development Department).

#gamedev|#indiedev|#ゲーム開発

For a game to be polished, it's essential for the developers to fine-tune every element, including the program, system (game loop, game status management, character status management, state flag bits, event flag bits, proper variable definitions, structure/class management, pointers, pointer lists, functions, function lists, interrupt handling, hit detection, coordinate calculations, camera coordinates, lighting adjustments, shadow mapping, improving processing speed in real space, screen space, and projection space, etc.), modeling, shading, UI, sprites, creation and adjustment of various effects, presentation adjustments, coordinate movement, fading, alpha ring blending, sound production, and sound effect production.

-----
Supplement
-----
On social media, you often see accounts trying to gain impressions or lying, posting things like, "The gaming industry is over! This was done with just one click and one line of prompts!" along with videos of existing, finished commercial games.
Frankly, these fake posts benefit no one and are not funny at all. Replies like, "This post isn't even funny as a joke," are common to these kinds of posts.
Instead of making such pointless posts that only waste viewers' time, it's far more worthwhile to look at the insights of people who bravely share the progress of their own games, even at the risk of their ideas being stolen, or, like Backer's posts, who complete a full stage and post it as an integrated benchmark (artistic benchmark).
At the very least, it's far better than looking at countless unfunny, fake posts that post things like, "The gaming industry is over! This was done with just one click and one line of prompts!" along with videos of existing, finished commercial games.

Backer | AAA programmer who has been active from the GBA era to the present.
I developed 2D and 3D games using C and C++ even before the days of the Engine.
Formerly CAPCOM Third Development Division (Console Game Development Department).

用 GPT-6 Astra 纯靠提示词生成单视口滚动交互网页，固定 Canvas 承载 12 步视差动效，不需要切页或重新加载。

entries.translated_prompt:
Use GPT-6 Astra to generate a single-viewport scrolling interactive webpage purely via prompts, with a fixed Canvas handling 12 steps of parallax animation without page switching or reloading.

The developer tested this with a 3D portfolio from a Tokyo studio, binding all 3D scenes and page animations to the scroll axis.
- The canvas is globally fixed to a single viewport; no routing jumps occur on the page, relying entirely on downward scrolling to drive the full animation sequence.
- 3D cards tilt and flip in 3D perspective as you scroll, smoothly presenting multiple projects with parallax transitions.
- Transitions use hard cuts and local pixel smearing to avoid traditional fade lag, with built-in constraints to prevent scroll hijacking.

Feeding the prompt set directly to the model generates this single-page 3D showcase scene driven primarily by scrolling.

entries.title: Build a 3D Action Game with GPT-6 Astra and Three.js
entries.description: A workflow description for creating a playable 3D action game similar to Dynasty Warriors using GPT-6 Astra for coding, combined with other AI tools for assets. The prompt focuses on integrating characters, scenes, and combat systems into a browser-based game.
entries.prompt:
如何用 AI 打造自己的三國無雙？！

剛好有一批快到期的重置額度要用掉，就想拿來挑戰看看，現在的 AI 到底能不能開發出一款真正可以玩的 3D 動作遊戲？！

於是我就結合了幾個 AI 工具：

- LLM： GPT-6 Astra，協助遊戲程式開發與整合
- 圖片生成： GPT Image、Nano Banana 2.1，負責角色與場景設計
- 3D 模型： Tripo H3.1，將角色圖片轉換成 3D 模型
- 角色配音： ElevenLabs，產生角色對白與配音

再透過 JavaScript 與 Three.js，把角色、場景、戰鬥系統整合成一款真正可以操作的 3D 遊戲！

遊戲取名為 《墨刃 Inkblade》，以鍾馗與中國志怪故事為背景。玩家扮演持劍的鍾馗，深入雨夜古寺與竹林，迎戰墨狼、神秘劍客與山魈，一路闖關揭開村民姓名被奪走的謎團。

最後把遊戲部署到免費的 Cloudflare Pages，不需要安裝，打開瀏覽器就能直接玩，手機也可以！
entries.translated_prompt:
How to build your own Dynasty Warriors with AI?!

I had some expiring reset quotas, so I wanted to challenge whether current AI can develop a truly playable 3D action game.

So I combined several AI tools:

- LLM: GPT-6 Astra, assisting with game programming and integration
- Image Generation: GPT Image, Nano Banana 2.1, responsible for character and scene design
- 3D Models: Tripo H3.1, converting character images into 3D models
- Character Voice: ElevenLabs, generating dialogue and voiceovers

Then through JavaScript and Three.js, integrate characters, scenes, and combat systems into a truly operable 3D game!

The game is named 'Inkblade', based on Zhong Kui and Chinese supernatural stories. Players control the sword-wielding Zhong Kui, venturing into rainy night ancient temples and bamboo forests, fighting ink wolves, mysterious swordsmen, and mountain demons, unlocking the mystery of villagers' stolen names.

Finally deploy the game to free Cloudflare Pages, no installation needed, play directly in the browser, also works on mobile!

entries.title: Teardown Tutorial for GPT-6 Astra
entries.description: A tutorial on how to use the 'teardown' skill with GPT-6 Astra to create interactive 3D mechanical websites. It provides specific instruction steps (prompts) for building a V8 engine example.
entries.prompt:
使用 teardown 的 V8 示例，构建一个可以离线打开的交互网页。保留完整机械结构、透明缸套、气门运动和实时图表。先运行原版，再修改。

把控制台改成中文，增加分层拆解、重新装配和单缸慢放按钮。保留浅色背景、金属材质和柔和投影。拆解后所有零件都要完整留在画面里。

在浏览器实际打开页面，测试旋转、缩放、暂停、拆解和复位。检查零件穿模、文字遮挡和画面裁切，发现问题就修复，再给我实际运行截图。
entries.translated_prompt:
Use the V8 example from teardown to build an interactive webpage that can be opened offline. Keep the complete mechanical structure, transparent cylinder liners, valve motion, and real-time charts. Run the original version first, then modify.

Change the console to Chinese, add buttons for layered disassembly, reassembly, and single-cylinder slow motion. Keep the light background, metallic materials, and soft shadows. All parts must remain fully visible within the frame after disassembly.

Actually open the page in a browser, test rotation, zoom, pause, disassembly, and reset. Check for part clipping, text occlusion, and screen cropping; fix any issues found, then give me actual runtime screenshots.

Build a full game world from a folder of reference images.

entries.title: Build Game World with GPT-6 Astra, Godot & Blender
entries.description: A detailed workflow for using GPT-6 Astra to build a 3D game world in Godot and Blender based on reference images. Includes steps for connecting MCPs, modeling props, and iterating on visuals.
entries.prompt:
build a game world from reference images with gpt-6 astra + godot + blender...

the ai matched the look from a folder of refs

here’s the workflow:

- step 1: collect images or videos of the look you want and put them in one folder (game/ref)
- step 2: connect godot mcp and blender mcp to codex
- step 3: have astra read the ref folder first so it understands the style before building anything
- step 4: install the dream-loop skill if you can: it helps the visuals match the refs more closely
- step 5: have astra model the props in blender: gate, market stalls, fountain, signposts, forge
- step 6: have it build the world in godot: castle, town square, forest paths, grass, fog
- step 7: walk through it, compare against the refs, fix what drifts

who does what:

> the ref folder: the style
> gpt-6 astra: reads the refs, models, builds, fixes
> blender: the props
> godot: the world, the light, the player

a folder of 10 good refs beats 10 paragraphs about “cozy fantasy vibes”.

entries.title: Inkshift Typography Sketchpad
entries.description: Description of a typography movement experiment built with GPT-6 Astra, allowing SVG export.
entries.prompt:
For one of my GPT-6 Astra builds, I wanted to explore typography through movement. The result is Inkshift.

A phrase can scatter, gather around the pointer or move into orbit. Freezing the motion turns a fleeting arrangement into something editable, with each letter's position, size and angle under your control.

The composition exports as an editable SVG, with the letters still stored as text. That makes the experiment useful beyond the moving canvas, although the same fonts are needed for a close match elsewhere.

It is a small sketchpad for finding an arrangement by moving the letters first, then refining what emerges.

entries.title: Cinematic Torii Shrine Scene Generation Prompt
entries.description: A comprehensive prompt for generating a photorealistic Japanese torii shrine scene using GPT-6 Astra, PixVerse, and Blender, including steps for concept art, 3D modeling, animation, and rendering.
entries.prompt: Create an original Japanese torii shrine scene using PixVerse and Blender. Complete these steps: Create the concept: Use PixVerse to generate a photoreal reference image. Lock the torii design, materials, lighting, and environment for consistency. Build the 3D scene: Create an editable textured model in Blender. Clean the topology, unwrap the UVs, and add suitable animation controls. Add movement: Include foreground leaves that partially obscure the wide shots, gently moving foliage, and birds flying visibly across the scene. Animate the cameras: Create a 12-second sequence with three shots: an arcing approach, a lateral detail shot, and a rising pullback. Keep movement smooth and framing clear. Render in Blender: Export a native camera video and a separate neutral gray clay reference video using the same animation. Save them beside the Blender project. Generate the photoreal film: Use PixVerse Seedance with the gray video for camera and action reference and the unchanged photoreal image for appearance. Generate a 1080p, 16:9 video with only natural environmental sounds—wind, rustling leaves, and bird wings. No music or voices. Check and deliver: Review every shot for consistent design, photoreal textures, visible birds, smooth motion, and correct audio. Fix issues within the approved budget and document remaining limitations. Save the editable Blender project, videos, reference image, and a brief production assessment in the same folder. Key points: Never use the colored low-poly video as the Seedance reference. Check the entire film, especially the final wide shot.

entries.title: UE5 Boss Fight Game Creation Workflow with GPT-6 Astra
entries.description: A detailed workflow for creating a playable UE5 boss fight game using GPT-6 Astra via Unreal MCP. The prompt instructs the AI to connect to UE5, design combat mechanics (parry, stamina, rage mode), use existing assets, and iteratively refine gameplay feel based on user feedback.
entries.prompt:
第一步，先把 Astra 和 UE5 连起来，再把想做的东西说清楚。
这一步最关键的是 MCP。简单说，它就是一个"插件桥"，接上以后 Astra 就能直接操作虚幻引擎：建蓝图、改参数、摆场景、跑游戏看效果，不用我们在编辑器里一个个点。
我用的是 UE 5.8 自带的官方插件 Unreal MCP，免费，在插件里搜"Unreal MCP"勾上、重启编辑器就能用，官方文档链接放评论区了👇
我这种没接触过UE界面的人，全靠它了😂 没有 MCP 的话，AI 只能通过Python代码或者给你一堆代码和步骤让你自己操作。
连好之后，我先跟 Astra 聊了很久：想要什么体验、主角有哪些招、Boss 怎么打、参考哪些游戏（比如只狼、战神、黑神话等等）。
最后定了一个核心玩法：精准招架不掉体力，还能攒"势"，攒满了放大招。
想清楚再动手，后面加东西不用推倒重来。

第二步，人物和动画别让 AI 从零做，直接用现成素材。
AI 现在最不擅长的就是人物建模和动画，自己做出来基本是灾难。
我用的是 Epic 在 Fab 上免费放出来的《Paragon》素材：主角、Boss、场景、大部分动作都是现成的，质量很高。
素材交给 Astra，让它去做它擅长的事。

第三步，系统和逻辑全交给 Astra。
战斗系统、技能、体力和数值、Boss 的 AI，基本都是它写的。
Boss 会看距离和朝向来出招，连招是一套一套编好的，半血还会进入狂暴换一套打法。这些我自己一行代码都没写😂
第四步，最花时间的是调手感。
跑起来很快，但第一版打起来很僵硬，一点都不爽，特效也做的不好。
后面几天基本就是：我自己一遍遍打，告诉它哪里不对，它改，再打。
小技巧：反馈一定要说具体，"出完招收不回来，要等很久才能动"就比"手感不好"有用得多。
第五步，音效是让AI根据你需要的音效从现有游戏素材里剪的，混好音再放进去。
entries.translated_prompt:
Step 1: Connect Astra to UE5 and clearly state what you want to build.
The key here is MCP. Simply put, it's a 'plugin bridge'. Once connected, Astra can directly operate Unreal Engine: create blueprints, change parameters, set up scenes, run the game to see effects, without us clicking around in the editor one by one.
I used the official Unreal MCP plugin built into UE 5.8, which is free. Just search for 'Unreal MCP' in the plugins, check it, and restart the editor to use it.
For someone like me who has never touched the UE interface, this was everything. Without MCP, the AI can only provide Python code or steps for you to do manually.
After connecting, I chatted with Astra for a long time: what experience I wanted, what moves the protagonist has, how the Boss fights, and reference games (like Sekiro, God of War, Black Myth, etc.).
Finally, we defined a core mechanic: precise parry doesn't drain stamina but builds up 'Momentum', which triggers a special move when full.
Think clearly before acting so you don't have to redo things later.

Step 2: Don't let AI model characters/animations from scratch; use ready-made assets.
AI is currently worst at character modeling and animation; doing it from scratch is usually a disaster.
I used the free 'Paragon' assets released by Epic on Fab: protagonist, Boss, scene, and most animations are ready-made and high quality.
Hand the assets to Astra and let it do what it's good at.

Step 3: Leave all systems and logic to Astra.
The combat system, skills, stamina/stats, and Boss AI were basically written by it.
The Boss attacks based on distance and orientation, combos are pre-programmed sequences, and it enters a rage phase at half health with a different attack pattern. I didn't write a single line of code myself.
Step 4: Tuning the 'game feel' took the most time.
It ran quickly, but the first version felt stiff and unsatisfying, and VFX were poor.
The next few days were mostly: I played repeatedly, told it what was wrong, it fixed it, and I played again.
Tip: Feedback must be specific. 'Can't recover after finishing an attack, wait too long to move' is much more useful than 'bad game feel'.
Step 5: Sound effects were cut by the AI from existing game assets based on my needs, then mixed and inserted.

entries.title: Build Playable 3D Hunting Game with AI Workflow
entries.description: Detailed workflow prompt for creating a 3D island hunting game demo using GPT-6 Astra (Codex), Tripo3D, Blender, and Claude Opus 5.5, covering asset generation, modeling, and gameplay implementation.
entries.prompt:
一开始，我先把想做的游戏和需要的素材告诉 Codex：荒岛狩猎，找到电台联系外界，需要什么样的人物、武器、动物，以及大致想要的场景效果。
接下来就让它操作电脑，它自己去生成了图片，然后在Tripo 里生成了一堆 3D 模型。
该拆分的都进行了拆分，该绑骨骼的都绑了骨骼。
生成模型之后，codex 继续操作 Blender，完成减面、组装，顺便做了基础场景的建模。
等基本场景成形，Opus 5.5 打磨细节。
entries.translated_prompt:
First, I told Codex the game concept and required assets: an island hunting game where you find a radio to contact the outside world, specifying needed characters, weapons, animals, and the general desired scene effects.
Then let it operate the computer; it generated images itself, then created a bunch of 3D models in Tripo.
It split parts as needed and rigged bones where necessary.
After generating the models, Codex continued to operate Blender, completing decimation, assembly, and basic scene modeling.
Once the basic scene was formed, Opus 5.5 polished the details.

entries.title: Decryption Game UI Design
entries.description: Detailed process of designing a WebGL interface for a decryption game using GPT-6 Astra for modeling and Fable 5 for animations.
entries.prompt:
事情是这样的，几年前和同事、朋友们沉迷《谍报风云》（一个类似谁是卧底的猜词游戏）时就想把它搬到线上，摸鱼的时候随时来一把。所以最早我手搓了一个聊天 Bot（那时还没有 AI）作为主持人，支持在 QQ 频道和 discord 上直接玩。但纯文字 UI 总觉得差点意思，于是想做一套 WebUI。只是它到底该长什么样，我一直没设计出来，项目也就搁着了。

时间回到现在，最近的模型在 3D 建模上似乎能力越来越强，之前也试过用 Kimi-K3 和 Fable5 去尝试做一下，但设计出来的东西仍然过于基础。

直到 GPT 6 Astra 出来，这次它在 3D 建模上的提升不是一般的大，所以才有机会一点点打磨出现在这套基于 WebGL 的界面 -- 这是我想象中的，如果真的存在一个真实的加解密游戏机器，应该长的样子，也还做了一些额外的、很好玩的交互。

这个整个过程大概是：

1. 用 GPT-image 生成图片，先找到想要的视觉感觉。
2. 让 GPT 6 Astra 参考图片建模出初版。
3. 用 GPT 6 Astra 和 Kimi-K3 反复打磨模型细节（K3 基本是在拖后腿，也是各种返工）。
4. 不过 Astra 不是万能的，对于示波器、撕纸条这些复杂动画，最后还是靠 Fable 5 完成，在这些涉及数学和代码实现的动画实现里，它比 GPT 6 强的多的多。

模型还是要搭配着用。

最后，还加上了在线语音和 AI 队友，让大家可以直接在游戏里交流，也能在人不够的时候拿 AI 来凑数了，算是把这套线上游戏的工具箱补得更完整了。
几年前一直没做出来的东西，总算有了可以玩的样子。不过桌游还是要线下玩，推荐大家买一个《谍报风云》感受一下。

线上游玩：https://t.co/LynqYrKuTf
代码地址：https://t.co/nmKxjzqPxQ
entries.translated_prompt:
Here is the situation: A few years ago, when my colleagues and friends were obsessed with "Spyfall" (a word-guessing game similar to Who's the Undercover), I wanted to bring it online so we could play a round whenever we had free time at work. So initially, I manually built a chat bot (before AI was mainstream) as the host, supporting direct play on QQ channels and Discord. But the pure text UI always felt lacking, so I wanted to create a WebUI. However, I never managed to design what it should look like, and the project was shelved.

Fast forward to now, recent models seem increasingly capable in 3D modeling. I previously tried using Kimi-K3 and Fable5 to attempt this, but the designs produced were still too basic.

Until GPT 6 Astra came out. Its improvement in 3D modeling this time was not just incremental, which gave me the opportunity to gradually polish the current WebGL-based interface—this is what I imagined a real encryption/decryption game machine would look like if it actually existed, along with some additional, very fun interactions.

The entire process was roughly:

1. Use GPT-image to generate images first to find the desired visual feel.
2. Have GPT 6 Astra reference the images to model an initial version.
3. Use GPT 6 Astra and Kimi-K3 repeatedly to refine model details (K3 was mostly dragging things down, resulting in various reworks).
4. However, Astra isn't omnipotent; for complex animations like oscilloscopes and tearing paper strips, Fable 5 ultimately completed them. In these animation implementations involving math and code, it is much stronger than GPT 6.

Models still need to be used in combination.

Finally, I added online voice and AI teammates, allowing everyone to communicate directly in the game, and also enabling AI to fill in when there aren't enough players, making the toolbox for this online game more complete.
Something that couldn't be made years ago finally has a playable form. However, board games are best played offline; I recommend everyone buy a copy of "Spyfall" to experience it.

Play online: https://t.co/LynqYrKuTf
Code repository: https://t.co/nmKxjzqPxQ

entries.title: Marble Computer Prompt: Astra vs Opus
entries.description: A detailed prompt for building a 3D marble computer in HTML/Three.js, explicitly shared as the input for both GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5.
entries.prompt:
Build a single self-contained HTML file: a 3D marble computer, in the spirit of Wintergatan's marble machine and the Digi-Comp II, that adds two 4-bit numbers using nothing but marbles falling through mechanical toggles.

Hard rules:

1. One HTML file. Three.js from https://t.co/KCQbEZLusb via an import map, plus its OrbitControls addon. No other libraries, no physics engine, no external assets.

2. The mechanism is the computer. Each bit of the result is stored in a two-state toggle (flip-flop) that a marble physically flips as it passes. Carries happen because a marble leaving one toggle rolls on to the next. Do not compute the answer in JavaScript arithmetic anywhere. The displayed result must be read from the toggle states after the last marble stops.

3. Marbles move along tracks with believable gravity and timing. Nothing teleports. You may script motion along paths, but every toggle flip must be caused by a marble arriving at it.

4. Input: two rows of four switches (A and B, 0 to 15), set by clicking. A lever labelled RUN releases the marbles. A counter shows how many marbles have fallen.

5. Output: a row of five result toggles, most significant bit on the left, and a readout that shows the binary and decimal value read from those toggles.

6. A DEMO button runs 5+6, then 9+7, then 15+15, resetting between runs, so it can be screen-recorded without touching anything.

7. Looks: a wooden board, brass toggles, glass marbles, warm studio lighting, soft shadows, a slow camera that follows the busiest part of the machine. It should look good in a square 1080x1080 recording.

8. Short click sounds via the Web Audio API when a toggle flips, started only after the first user click.

9. It must run at 60 fps on a normal laptop and have no console errors.

Output only the complete HTML file.

entries.title: Automated 3D Character Pipeline
entries.description: A prompt instructing GPT-6 Astra to take over a computer and execute a full 3D character creation workflow, from concept design in Higgsfield to rigging and animation.
entries.prompt:

1. 使用 Higgsfield Soul 2.0 设计角色概念，

7. 评估模型是否达到制作就绪状态，

3. Import it into Blender,

4. Retopologize the mesh,

5. Create UV maps,

6. Create a character rig,

entries.title: GPT-6 Astra Video Generation Pipeline Prompt
entries.description: A detailed prompt for GPT-6 Astra to create a dramatic video clip of the Lusaka Freedom statue coming to life, involving web search for references, image generation with GPT Image 2.5, video generation with Seedance, and CapCut editing.
entries.prompt: I want a 45 sec dramatic clip of the Lusaka's Freedom statue. Search the web for reference images to use. The shot zooms in on the face and the bronze statue cames to life maintaining its bronze features. After coming to life, the bronze statue jumps of it's mount and drops his bondange chains. He then kicks open the gate and walks out. The camera then zooms in on him as he says "I know what you are planning, don't do it!!" His voice must be deep and ominous with a growl layer. It should have scarly elements. I want this in 9:16 aspect ratio. Video generation should be done in Krea ai using Seedance 2.5 and image generation should be done with GPT Image 2.5. When the video clips are done, use CapCut on my computer to join them. Create the entire pipeline using my Ai video skill. Show me the pipeline before proceeding.

entries.prompt:
请直接制作一个可以在浏览器中实时交互的高完成度 3D 景观网页。

主题：日式樱花山谷。
使用 HTML、CSS、JavaScript 实现。不要生成图片，不要只给设计方案，
不要用一张背景图加视差效果冒充 3D。我要的是实际可运行、可游览的成品。

【一、作品定位】

这是一片完整、连续、有远近层次的山谷景观，
不是孤立的小摆件、悬浮岛、带底座的沙盘，也不是单纯的技术演示。

风格是现代精细体素 / voxel art：
保留立方体几何的造型语言，但画面应高分辨率、抗锯齿、光影细腻。
不要复古低分辨率像素化，不要粗大积木堆砌，不要给画面套像素滤镜。

视觉质量优先。宁可少几个功能，也不要牺牲构图、材质和光照。

【二、参考图的使用方式】

如果附有参考图，请先理解它的构图层次、尺度、光线和色彩关系。
仅借鉴氛围与视觉语言，重新设计场景，
不要照搬建筑、树木、山体和道路的位置，不要 1:1 复刻。

参考图不是网页里的背景素材。场景本身必须由真实 3D 几何构成。

【三、场景构图】

默认打开时就应呈现一幅完整、有吸引力的画面，
不需要用户先旋转镜头才能找到好看的角度。

采用透视相机，而不是沙盘式等距俯视相机。
画面有明确的前景、中景、远景：

前景：
一株有存在感的古老樱花树，配合岩石、草木、石灯笼和少量落花，
形成画面边缘的自然框景，但不能挡住河流、桥和主要建筑。

中景：
一条蜿蜒河流引导视线进入画面，红色木桥横跨河面；
村落、茶屋、神社和小径顺着地势分布，建筑之间有真实的通行关系。
地面有起伏、岸线和自然过渡，不是平面上均匀摆放模型。

远景：
山坡上的多层塔、不同距离的森林和山脊，以及远处的雪山。
用尺度变化、遮挡、冷暖变化和空气透视表现距离，
而不是仅仅把远处物体缩小。

不要把所有元素均匀铺满。需要主次、疏密、留白和清楚的视觉焦点。

【四、造型与画面质量】

樱花树：
树干有转折、分叉和根部，树冠由不规则花簇组成，
有间隙、厚薄变化和可见枝条。不要做成几个规则球体或方块团。

建筑：
屋顶有层叠瓦片、挑檐、梁柱和窗格；
不同建筑有用途、体量和高度差异，不要复制同一栋房子铺满山谷。

地形：
岸边有湿润石块、草丛和植被过渡。
避免过于规律的台阶、重复条纹、棋盘格和明显的程序生成网格。

水面：
必须能够反映周围景物，具有适度的波纹、深浅变化和岸边过渡。
尽量使用实际场景反射；需要性能降级时也应保持视觉可信。
不要用闪烁噪声、强烈扭曲或一整块蓝色平面代替水。

细节：
可以有少量锦鲤、落花、萤火虫、瀑布和远处飞鸟，
但都应服务于氛围，不能让画面显得嘈杂。
不要为了宣称模型数量而堆砌细节。

【五、色彩与氛围】

默认是蓝调时刻：
偏冷的山谷与远山，柔和的粉色樱花，温暖但不过曝的灯笼和窗光。
暖光集中在有人活动的地方，不要把整个环境染成橙色。

需要柔和阴影、物体接触处的明暗、合理的曝光、
克制的泛光、抗锯齿和有距离层次的薄雾。

避免发白、灰蒙、过度饱和、满屏浓雾、过曝灯光和明显锯齿。
方块几何可以清晰，但渲染本身不能粗糙。

另提供“清晨”和“雨中”两种氛围；
切换时应同步改变天空、环境光、雾和局部效果，
不是仅仅修改背景颜色。

【六、交互与界面】

提供四个经过设计的镜头：
山谷全景、河边低机位、寺庙小径、山坡俯瞰。
切换应平滑，每个镜头都需要有独立的构图价值。

基础交互：
鼠标拖动观察、滚轮缩放或前进，触屏支持拖动和双指缩放。
提供重置视角、隐藏界面和保存当前画面的功能。

可选增强：
自由探索、缓慢镜头巡游、环境音。
环境音默认关闭，只在用户主动点击后播放。
额外功能不能影响默认画面的完成度。

界面要克制、有设计感，以景观为主。
标题和控制条放在边缘，不遮挡视觉焦点。
桌面和手机都不能出现按钮越界、文字重叠或无法操作的问题。

【七、工程与性能】

允许使用 Three.js / WebGL，以及版本固定、互相兼容的 CDN 依赖。
优先使用成熟渲染能力，不要为了“零依赖”重写整套引擎。

自写的 HTML、CSS、JavaScript 尽量整理在一个 HTML 文件中。
景物由程序化几何和材质生成，不依赖外部图片或 3D 模型资源。

重复物体采用适合的批量或实例化绘制方式；
合理控制细分、阴影、反射和渲染分辨率。
提供高画质和轻量模式，手机默认使用较轻设置。
不要靠无限增加体素数量换取细节。

加入加载提示、WebGL 不支持时的提示和必要的错误处理。
没有开启声音时不要自动播放；尊重减少动态效果的系统偏好。

【八、交付前验收】

不要写完代码就立即交付。

如果当前环境支持浏览器运行和截图，请先实际打开页面，
检查默认镜头、四个视角、氛围切换、桌面和手机布局，
再根据截图修正明显的构图、曝光、遮挡和渲染问题。

重点检查：
是否存在空白画面、加载失败、控制台错误；
是否有穿模、闪烁、阴影条纹、过曝、水面异常；
默认画面是否真正像完整景观，而不是小型沙盘；
功能按钮是否实际可用，移动端是否越界。

可以使用浏览器截图验收，但不要调用图像生成工具。
没有完成的测试要如实说明，不要声称已经验证。

最终交付：
1. 实际存在、可以打开的 HTML 文件，或当前环境支持的交互预览。
2. 如能截图，附一张真实浏览器渲染截图。
3. 简短说明操作方式和必要的运行条件。

请直接完成制作；非关键细节自行作出一致的设计选择，
不要把可以自行解决的实现问题反复交给我决定。
entries.translated_prompt:
Please directly create a high-fidelity 3D landscape webpage that can be interacted with in real-time within a browser.

Theme: Japanese-style cherry blossom valley.
Implement using HTML, CSS, JavaScript. Do not generate images, do not just provide design proposals,
do not fake 3D with a background image plus parallax effects. I want an actual runnable, explorable product.

[1. Work Positioning]

This is a complete, continuous valley landscape with depth layers,
not isolated small ornaments, floating islands, sand tables with bases, or simple technical demos.

Style: Modern fine-grained voxel art:
Retain the modeling language of cubic geometry, but the screen should be high-resolution, anti-aliased, with delicate light and shadow.
No retro low-resolution pixelation, no crude block stacking, no pixel filters applied to the screen.

Visual quality first. Rather have fewer features than sacrifice composition, materials, and lighting.

[2. Usage of Reference Images]

If reference images are attached, please first understand their compositional hierarchy, scale, lighting, and color relationships.
Only borrow atmosphere and visual language, redesign the scene,
do not copy the positions of buildings, trees, mountains, and roads, do not replicate 1:1.

Reference images are not background assets for the webpage. The scene itself must be composed of real 3D geometry.

[3. Scene Composition]

The default view upon opening should present a complete, attractive picture,
without requiring users to rotate the camera to find a good angle first.

Use a perspective camera, not a sandbox-style isometric top-down camera.
The screen has clear foreground, midground, and background:

Foreground:
An ancient cherry tree with presence, accompanied by rocks, vegetation, stone lanterns, and some falling petals,
forming a natural frame at the edge of the screen, but without blocking the river, bridge, and main buildings.

Midground:
A winding river guides the gaze into the screen, with a red wooden bridge spanning the water;
villages, tea houses, shrines, and paths distributed along the terrain, with real traffic relationships between buildings.
The ground has undulations, shoreline, and natural transitions, not models evenly placed on a plane.

Background:
Multi-tiered towers on slopes, forests and ridges at different distances, and distant snow-capped mountains.
Express distance through scale changes, occlusion, warm/cold variations, and aerial perspective,
rather than simply shrinking distant objects.

Do not spread all elements evenly. Need primary/secondary, density/sparse, whitespace, and clear visual focus.

[4. Modeling and Screen Quality]

Cherry Trees:
Trunks have turns, forks, and roots; crowns consist of irregular flower clusters,
with gaps, thickness variations, and visible branches. Do not make them regular spheres or cube clumps.

Buildings:
Roofs have layered tiles, eaves, beams/columns, and window grids;
different buildings have differences in use, volume, and height, do not copy the same house to fill the valley.

Terrain:
Shorelines have wet stones, grass, and vegetation transitions.
Avoid overly regular steps, repeating stripes, checkerboards, and obvious procedural generation grids.

Water Surface:
Must reflect surrounding scenery, with moderate ripples, depth variations, and shore transitions.
Try to use actual scene reflections; if performance degradation is needed, maintain visual credibility.
Do not replace water with flickering noise, strong distortion, or a whole blue plane.

Details:
Can have some koi, falling petals, fireflies, waterfalls, and distant birds,
but all should serve the atmosphere, cannot make the screen look noisy.
Do not pile up details just to claim model count.

[5. Color and Atmosphere]

Default is Blue Hour:
Cool valleys and distant mountains, soft pink cherry blossoms, warm but not overexposed lantern and window lights.
Warm light concentrated where people are active, do not dye the entire environment orange.

Need soft shadows, light/dark at object contacts, reasonable exposure,
restrained bloom, anti-aliasing, and thin mist with distance layering.

Avoid whitening, grayness, oversaturation, full-screen thick fog, overexposed lights, and obvious aliasing.
Block geometry can be clear, but rendering itself cannot be rough.

Also provide "Morning" and "Rainy" atmospheres;
when switching, synchronously change sky, ambient light, fog, and local effects,
not just modifying background color.

[6. Interaction and Interface]

Provide four designed cameras:
Valley Panorama, Low Riverbank Camera, Temple Path, Slope Overlook.
Switching should be smooth, each camera needs independent compositional value.

Basic Interaction:
Mouse drag to observe, scroll wheel to zoom or move forward, touch screen supports drag and pinch-to-zoom.
Provide reset view, hide interface, and save current screen functions.

Optional Enhancements:
Free exploration, slow camera tour, ambient sound.
Ambient sound off by default, only play after user actively clicks.
Extra functions cannot affect the completeness of the default screen.

Interface should be restrained, designed, with landscape as the main subject.
Titles and control bars on edges, not blocking visual focus.
Desktop and mobile cannot have button overflow, text overlap, or unoperatable issues.

[7. Engineering and Performance]

Allow use of Three.js / WebGL, and version-pinned, mutually compatible CDN dependencies.
Prioritize mature rendering capabilities, do not rewrite the entire engine for "zero dependency".

Self-written HTML, CSS, JavaScript try to organize in one HTML file.
Scenery generated by procedural geometry and materials, not relying on external images or 3D model resources.

Repeated objects use suitable batch or instanced drawing methods;
Reasonably control subdivision, shadows, reflections, and rendering resolution.
Provide high-quality and lightweight modes, mobile defaults to lighter settings.
Do not trade infinite voxel increase for detail.

Add loading prompts, WebGL unsupported prompts, and necessary error handling.
Do not autoplay when sound is not enabled; respect system preference for reduced motion.

[8. Pre-delivery Acceptance]

Do not deliver immediately after writing code.

If the current environment supports browser running and screenshots, please actually open the page first,
Check default camera, four views, atmosphere switching, desktop and mobile layout,
Then correct obvious composition, exposure, occlusion, and rendering issues based on screenshots.

Key Checks:
Whether there are blank screens, loading failures, console errors;
Whether there are clipping, flickering, shadow banding, overexposure, water surface anomalies;
Whether the default screen truly looks like a complete landscape, not a small sand table;
Whether function buttons are actually usable, whether mobile side has overflow.

Can use browser screenshot acceptance, but do not call image generation tools.
Incomplete tests must be stated honestly, do not claim verified.

Final Delivery:
1. An actually existing, openable HTML file, or interactive preview supported by the current environment.
2. If screenshots possible, attach one real browser rendering screenshot.
3. Brief explanation of operation method and necessary runtime conditions.

Please complete the production directly; make consistent design choices for non-critical details yourself,
do not repeatedly hand implementation problems that can be self-resolved back to me for decision.

entries.title: Reusable Rocket Factory 3D Sim

entries.title: GPT-6 Astra Star Wars Three.js Worlds
entries.description: A benchmark comparing GPT-6 Astra against other models on generating three distinct Star Wars-themed 3D web experiences using Three.js. The prompt instructs the model to create single-file HTML applications with procedural textures, cinematic camera paths, and specific physics simulations for Death Star, Coruscant, and Kamino environments.
entries.prompt:
Create a single HTML file containing a Three.js (v0.170) scene for {argument name="location" default="Death Star"}. Use only CDN links for Three.js; generate all textures procedurally in code (no external images or model files). Implement an auto-playing cinematic sequence with a shot timeline, letterbox effects, and fades. Ensure zero console errors on first run.

For {argument name="location" default="Death Star"}:
- A slow orbital approach with star destroyers for scale.
- The corridor into the throne room.
- The station over a planet's horizon.
- The superlaser: eight tributary beams, one green shot, a shockwave ring, and thousands of instanced fragments.

For {argument name="location" default="Coruscant"}:
- The planet from orbit as a circuit board of glowing hubs.
- A daytime flythrough between towers, under a bridge, and past the senate dome.
- A neon night district with a highway of light trails.

For {argument name="location" default="Kamino"}:
- An ocean world under storm clouds.
- Tipoca city on stilts with Gerstner waves, GPU rain, and lightning.
- A glass walkway over a hall of marching clones.

entries.title: 3D Submarine Reef Game
entries.description: Detailed description of a browser-based 3D game featuring a submarine diving through a reef, built by GPT-6 Astra in one prompt. Includes specific visual elements like depth meters, coin counters, fish behavior, and camera controls.
entries.prompt:
A submarine dives through a living 3D reef. GPT-6 Astra built it in one prompt.

No engine, no install. The fish, the coral, the sunbeams and the controls all run in a browser tab.

The same test made another frontier model swim backwards.

Watch the depth meter in the bottom-left corner. It starts at 5.3 m and passes 13 m as the little yellow sub sinks toward the sand. Top right, the coin counter keeps climbing from 2,836 to over 3,100.

Around it, a whole reef: light rays through the surface, mossy boulders, pink fan coral, and a school of goldfish that follows the sub around.

At 0:10 a blue fish with a narwhal horn cruises by. At 0:16 an orange one swims right up to the camera. Hit pause and the game tells you to "Take a breath."

Now the comparison.

Grok 4.7 got the exact same test. On its first try, the submarine and every fish swam backwards. On the second, the camera ended up inside the sub's hull.

Anyone can generate a fish. Knowing which way it faces is the hard part.

That's why this test is brutal. The model has to keep track of front and back, what's above and below, and where the camera sits, with no 3D tool to check its work. GPT-6 Astra is being called world class at exactly this kind of spatial reasoning, and this clip is the evidence.

To be clear, "one-shot" means one prompt and no fixes, and this is a small demo, not a store-ready game. But a year ago, one prompt got you a spinning cube.

Is 3D the first place GPT-6 Astra has a real lead, or will the others catch up within a month?

entries.title: Graphite Pleat Dress Generation Prompt for GPT-6 Astra
entries.description: The user explicitly shares the instructions given to GPT-6 Astra to generate a dress in Blender: 'graphite pleats, a copper belt and quiet studio lighting'. This is a valid 3D asset creation prompt.
entries.prompt:
GPT-6 Astra just made a dress inside Blender from code

I asked for graphite pleats, a copper belt and quiet studio lighting. It wrote the Python that built an editable garment with 48 physical folds, 12 UV panels, materials, a camera and a looped hem animation

This 4-second clip is the first look-development test. The movement is art-directed through shape keys, so cloth physics still comes later

The render is only the visible part. The .blend file, UV layout and source script are all saved, which means I can keep refining the silhouette instead of starting over.

entries.prompt: Build an entire city inside the ENTER key of this keyboard photo. Plan the scene and camera setup in Blender first.

entries.prompt: Create a real-time moving ocean in the browser using WebGPU, Three.js, and TSL. Include rolling swells, fine ripples, and sunset reflections broken by the wave surface. Implement real-time controls for wave size, day/night lighting, and camera drift.

entries.title: End-to-End 3D Roaming Video of Macondo in Blender
entries.description: A detailed workflow for generating a 3D roaming video of the town of Macondo from 'One Hundred Years of Solitude' using GPT-6 Astra. The process involves Codex calling Blender MCP for modeling, automatic camera routing, and integration with ChatCut and Eleven Music for editing and audio.
entries.prompt: Create a 3D roaming video of the town of Macondo from 'One Hundred Years of Solitude' in Blender. Use Codex to call the Blender MCP interface to model and refine the environment autonomously. Select a camera route within Blender and assemble seamless roaming shots switching between white models, raw models, and rendered frames. Edit the footage with ChatCut and generate a soundtrack matching the South American magical realism style using Eleven Music.

To recreate the room shown in the second image, identify and create the missing 3D model parts (such as curtains) and place them correctly.

Implement real-time paint customization, cinematic lighting, 360-degree exploration, and animated wind-tunnel airflow effects.

entries.title: GPT-6 Astra 3D Animation Studio Build
entries.description: Describes a developer building a 3D animation studio tool using GPT-6 Astra. It details the workflow (Mixamo + Kimodo) and mentions a specific trick/prompt for generating dodge rolls ('person rolling on the ground...'), but this is embedded in a narrative description of a complex pipeline rather than a standalone, copy-paste ready prompt for a new user. However, the specific instruction for the motion generation is extractable as a niche 3D/game asset prompt.
entries.prompt:
One dev built his own 3D animation studio in about a week of prompting.

Four live viewports, ghost trails, 79-joint rigs, an 85-clip motion library. All made with GPT-6 Astra.

The strange part: he has no idea what game it's for yet.

Watch the faded copies trailing each character. Every ghost is an earlier frame, so the whole move sits on screen at once. The horned demon at 0:12 shows it best.

The pipeline is two free sources glued together → Mixamo for stock motion, Kimodo (NVIDIA's open motion model) for everything in between.

Then he shared the trick.

Grab one frame of an idle pose. Set it as both the first and the last frame. Put a pose of someone on the floor in the middle and prompt "person rolling on the ground to the right" over 2 seconds.

Out comes a Dark Souls style dodge roll that starts and ends in the exact same stance. Flip the direction in the prompt and you have the other side.

The cost? Roughly one week of usage on the Lite version of the model. Earlier this month he used the same AI to finish a whole game in a few days.

The game doesn't exist yet. The studio for it already does.

To be clear, you can't download this. It's built around his own workflow, and he says the AI wasn't the hard part. Making the UI feel logical was.

Solo devs building their own tools instead of buying them: the new normal, or a rabbit hole that stops games from shipping?

entries.title: Recreating Visual Styles in Godot and Blender with Astra
entries.description: A step-by-step guide on using GPT-6 Astra connected to Godot and Blender via MCP to analyze reference folders and recreate visual styles. The goal is a walkable third-person world with specific environmental elements.
entries.prompt:
GPT-6 ASTRA, WIRED INTO GODOT AND BLENDER, IS GETTING CLOSER TO RECREATING A VISUAL STYLE DIRECTLY FROM REFERENCES.

▪ STEP ONE: Gather images and videos that capture the exact aesthetic you want, then place them together in a dedicated folder like "Game/Ref".

▪ STEP TWO: Connect Godot MCP and Blender MCP to Codex, giving the AI direct control and access to both the game engine and 3D workflow.

▪ STEP THREE: Have Astra analyze everything inside the "Ref" folder, allowing it to understand the colors, atmosphere, environments, shapes, lighting, and overall visual language.

▪ STEP FOUR: If available, install the Dream-loop skill. It can help the agent iterate more effectively and push the final visuals closer to the reference material.

The outcome?

A fully walkable third-person world featuring a forest path, a fog-covered valley, a massive castle entrance with a working drawbridge, and a town square centered around a fountain — all connected into one continuous exploration experience.

entries.title: Improve Web Design Workflow with Codex Mockups
entries.description: Guide on using Codex (powered by GPT-6 Astra) to generate visual website mockups before coding, including a starting prompt structure.
entries.prompt:
how to improve GPT-6 Astra / Codex's ability to design and code websites

I've been using this approach since GPT Image was released, and the results have kept improving with 2 and 2.5

the idea is to have Codex generate visual mockups of the website before building it, whether you're reimagining an existing page or starting with an idea from scratch

you can review the layout, give feedback and agree on the design before it starts writing the frontend

here's how to use it:

1. give Codex the idea and your context

explain who the website is for, what it needs to communicate and what you want someone to do when they visit

include the material you already have:

> your page copy and product information
> brand guidelines, fonts, colors and assets
> screenshots of the existing page if you're redesigning
> references with notes on what you like about each one

have it ask about anything missing before generating the mockup

for an existing website, ask it to inspect the current implementation too, including components and functionality that need to stay

2. ask it to generate the design first

be explicit that you want an image mockup to review before implementation

a starting prompt:

> use imagegen to create a website mockup from this brief and the attached references
> use the supplied copy, brand assets and product information
> show the page layout, typography, imagery and calls to action, and wait for my feedback before writing code

you can request different visual directions if you're still exploring, with each version changing something meaningful like the layout or use of imagery

3. work through the mockup together

review it as a page someone needs to understand and use

> is the main message clear?
> does the layout guide attention toward the intended action?
> is the text readable?
> does the design fit your brand?
> are there generic sections or invented details that should be removed?

give specific feedback on the image, such as increasing the space around the headline, reducing decorative elements or moving the product example higher on the page

ask it to revise the chosen mockup while preserving the parts you've approved

4. turn the approved mockup into a build plan

have Codex identify the sections, reusable components and assets needed to implement the design

agree on what happens when someone interacts with it, including navigation, forms, buttons and any loading or error states

also define how the layout should adapt to mobile, because a desktop mockup leaves those decisions open

save the approved image and your decisions in the project so Codex can refer to them during the build

5. find relevant UX / UI skills before building

you can find these in skill directories and through recommendations on X, UI Skills is one example to explore

https://t.co/NSjtzraOfs

give your Grok Bot the project brief and have it research which skills are popular and worth considering for your stack

ask it to check what each skill does, who maintains it and whether its instructions fit the website you're building

that could include skills for:

> frontend design and component patterns
> accessibility and responsive layouts
> animation and interaction design
> reviewing the finished UI

review the shortlist, then give Codex the selected skills alongside your design system and approved mockup before implementation

6. build the page from that reference

ask Codex to implement the approved design using your project's existing stack and components where appropriate

keep headings, buttons and forms as working website elements, with illustrations and other generated visuals saved as separate assets

a useful implementation prompt:

> build the approved mockup as a responsive page
> preserve its layout, spacing, typography and visual hierarchy, use the approved copy and implement the interactions we agreed
> flag anything that needs a design decision before changing it

7. compare the rendered website with the mockup

have Codex open the implemented page in a browser and capture screenshots at desktop and mobile sizes

compare those screenshots with the approved design and work through the differences

check spacing, font sizes, image proportions, alignment and text wrapping, then test the links, forms and keyboard navigation

after you've reviewed the page, save the final screenshots and reusable design rules with the project for the next page you build

entries.title: 15 Rules for Using Astra in ChatGPT/Codex
entries.description: A guide on how to effectively use the Astra model (GPT-6 Astra) in ChatGPT Work and Codex. While it contains example prompts like 'Deliver a ranked comparison...', these are illustrative snippets for general productivity tasks, not a specific creative generation prompt for image/3D/web creation as per the strict filter requirements for reusable author-written instructions for this model's scope.
entries.prompt:
"Deliver a ranked comparison. Show the sample size for each group. Flag conclusions based on very few posts."
No "think step by step". Be direct instead.

8). Attach files. Explain their role.
↳ Exact prompt: "Use the brand guide for style and the product brief for facts. If they disagree, flag the conflict first."
Evidence, template, or instructions: Astra can't tell.

9). Say which decisions need your input.
↳ Astra asks for clarification more than any model before. Useful to brainstorm but it gets very annoying for the tasks you already had a solution for. Name the 2-3 questions worth asking.

10). Let it handle the rest.
↳ Exact prompt: "Otherwise, complete the plan and list any assumptions at the end."

11). Specify tone, length & format.
↳ The default is overly perfect sentences. "600-800 words. Paragraphs of 2-3 sentences. Answer Greg's question in the first line."
My favorite trick: "Use ASD-STE100."

12). Add: "List your assumptions."
↳ You can catch its guesses very easily when it tries to fill the gap. Catch the misinformation early.

13). Correct its direction as it works.
↳ It is quite good at long tasks, while consuming tokens. So send a follow-up mid-task to see its plan & execution. Just like... a human?

14). Tell it exactly what to check.
↳ Exact prompt: "Before delivering, confirm the totals match the source, identify duplicates, and check every chart uses the correct date range."

15). Add: "Flag anything unresolved."
↳ This removes the fake "all done!" report. Unverified stays unverified.

entries.title: Fantasy Sword Specification Prompt
entries.description: A highly detailed technical specification/prompt for creating a fantasy sword in Blender via Python script, emphasizing silhouette, dimensions, materials, and UV mapping rules.
entries.prompt:
【AIに渡した剣の仕様書（そのまま貼り付け用・全文）】

これは「参照画像1枚から、AIにBlenderで3Dモデルを作らせる」ときに渡した仕様書です。
元は5つのファイルに分かれていたものを、1本のテキストにまとめ直しています。
このテキストをそのままAIに渡せば、同じ条件で作らせることができます。

■ 1. 何を作るか

ファンタジー風の装飾剣を1本。静的な3Dモデル（ゲーム用の小物、2Dスプライト化も想定）。

参照画像は正面1枚のみ。側面、斜め、背面はなし。

■ 2. 作り方の指定

・画像から3Dを推測するAI（TripoSRなど）は使わない。
・画像を観察して、Blender Pythonで部品ごとに直接造形する。
・元画像は変更しない。出力は新規フォルダーのみ。既存の完成版は上書きしない。
・参照画像を出力フォルダーへコピーし、絶対パスとSHA-256を記録する。
・造形内容はこの仕様書を優先し、画像は微調整に使う。
・背面や厚みなど見えない部分は「仮定」として記録する。
・実行していない項目を、検証済みと記録しない。

■ 3. 向きと全体寸法

単位はメートル。
柄頭が+Z、剣先が-Z。正面は-Y、右は+X。
剣先 z=0.00、柄頭の頂点 z=1.20。

全長 1.20
鍔の最大幅 0.34
刀身の最大幅 0.072
握りの外径 0.04
柄頭の最大幅 0.045

Z方向の配置
剣先 0.00
刀身の根元 0.89
鍔の中心 0.91
握りの開始 0.94
握りの終了 1.13
柄頭の基部 1.13
柄頭の頂点 1.20

※これらは設計値であり、実物の採寸ではありません。

■ 4. 部品（最低10種類に分ける）

blade（刀身）
両刃のまっすぐな刃。先端に向かってやや細くなる。
長さ0.89、根元幅0.072、中間幅0.056、先端手前0.02
厚みは根元0.012、中間0.008、先端手前0.003
断面はダイヤモンド／レンズ形のハイブリッド。中央が厚く、縁は薄く、研がれて見えること。

guard_center（中央の鍔）
金色。下向きのV字が刀身の根元へ伸びる。
幅0.085、高さ0.09、奥行0.022
中央に菱形の青い宝石を組み込む。宝石のまわりは面取りされた装飾枠。

guard_arm_left / guard_arm_right（鍔の左右の腕）
湾曲した腕。外側へ、やや下向き。
長さ0.127、厚み0.018、奥行0.016、先端の下がり0.015
先端に向かってわずかに広がり、面取りされたキャップで終わる。右は左のミラーでよい。

gem_frame（宝石の枠）
菱形の金枠。高さ0.05、幅0.03、奥行0.012
まわりの面よりわずかに浮かせる。

gem_blue（青い宝石）
面取りされた菱形の宝石。高さ0.028、幅0.016、奥行0.008
通常の距離で、はっきり青く見えること。

grip_core（握りの芯）
円柱〜ゆるい八角形。長さ0.19、直径0.034
表面は濃い茶色の革。シルエットはまっすぐ、中心を通す。

leather_wrap（革巻き）
交差する編み込み、または螺旋の帯。帯幅0.006、盛り上がり0.002
正面から見て、斜めの交差が見えること。

pommel_collar（柄頭の金具）
握りと柄頭の間の短い金の輪。高さ0.018、直径0.03

pommel（柄頭）
面取りされた錐状。高さ0.055、最大幅0.045、基部幅0.022
先端は尖った面で終わる。金属、または淡い結晶金属に見えること。

■ 5. 材質（色はRGB、0〜1）

blade_steel  色 0.72 / 0.74 / 0.77  金属1.0  粗さ0.28  （磨きすぎない、ブラシ仕上げ）
guard_gold   色 0.74 / 0.62 / 0.30  金属1.0  粗さ0.24  （暖かみのあるファンタジー金）
gem_blue     色 0.16 / 0.33 / 0.70  金属0.0  粗さ0.08  （透過なしの不透明な宝石でよい）
leather_dark 色 0.22 / 0.14 / 0.10  金属0.0  粗さ0.72  （濃い茶の革）
leather_wrap 色 0.18 / 0.11 / 0.08  金属0.0  粗さ0.76  （芯より少し暗く）
pommel_metal 色 0.66 / 0.63 / 0.58  金属1.0  粗さ0.30  （明るめの金属）

■ 6. 造形の規則

・細部より、まずシルエットを優先する。
・画像のハイライトや影を、そのまま立体にしない。
・刀身の縁は、中央よりはっきり薄くする。
・鍔は平板にせず、層があるように見せる。
・背面は正面の作りを流用してよい（参照がないため）。
・部品には役割の分かる名前を付け、編集できる状態を保つ。
・n-gonはGLB書き出しの直前にだけ三角化する。

■ 7. UVとテクスチャ

・全メッシュにUVを作り、重なりを避ける。
・2048×2048のアトラス1枚にまとめる。
・焼くのはBase Color、Roughness、Metallic、Normalの4種。
・GLBにはテクスチャを内蔵し、外部ファイルに依存させない。

■ 8. 品質の目安

三角形数は15,000〜45,000が目安。
ただしこれは目安であって、下限を満たすためだけに形を増やさないこと。
用途は静的なゲーム用アセットと、複数角度からのスプライト化。

■ 9. 実行の順番

1. 出力フォルダーを新規作成する。既存の完成版は上書きしない。
2. 参照画像を出力先へコピーする。
3. SHA-256を再計算し、一致とローカル絶対パスを記録する。
4. 仕様に従って造形スクリプトを実装する。
5. Blenderのバックグラウンド実行で、編集可能な原本とプレビューを作る。
6. プレビューを見て、シルエットと接続の修正を優先して行う。
7. UV展開とPBR焼き込みを行う。
8. GLBを書き出す。
9. 空のシーンへ読み込み直して検証する。
10. 実測値と実際の検証結果で記録を更新する。

注意
・初回から過剰なディテールを入れない。
・刀身、鍔、柄、宝石、柄頭の比率を優先する。
・正面1枚しかないので、厚みと背面は保守的に設計する。
・寸法や形状を変えたら、変更内容と理由を短く記録する。
・形が決まる前に、最終の焼き込みや動画制作へ進まない。
・未実行や失敗は、そのままの状態として記録する。

■ 10. 合格の基準

・全体のシルエットが参照画像と大きく一致している。
・長短の比、鍔の広がり、柄の太さ、宝石の位置が合っている。
・斜めから見て平板に見えない。
・部品の間に、意図しない隙間、貫通、黒い穴がない。
・金属、革、宝石が材質として見分けられる。
・GLBを読み込み直しても、形、UV、法線、接線、質感が保たれている。

■ 11. 書き出す前に必ず確かめること

・GLBのヘッダーとデータ長が正しい。
・すべての面に、位置、法線、UV、接線がある。
・Base Color、Metallic/Roughness、Normalが入っている。
・画像がGLBの中に埋め込まれている。
・座標に異常な値がない。
・孤立した頂点や辺がない。
・部品数、三角形数、サイズを記録に残す。
・読み込み直したGLBで、正面、斜め、背面、細部を描画して目で見る。

失敗したまま完成扱いにしない。未実行、失敗、合格を区別して記録する。
entries.translated_prompt:
【Sword Specification Document for AI (Full Text for Copy-Paste)】

This is the specification document used when asking an AI to create a 3D model in Blender from a single reference image.
The original content was split into five files, which have been consolidated into this single text.
Passing this text directly to an AI will allow it to generate results under the same conditions.

■ 1. What to Create

One fantasy-style decorative sword. A static 3D model (intended as a game prop, also suitable for 2D sprite conversion).

Only one front-facing reference image is provided. No side, diagonal, or back views are available.

■ 2. Creation Method Specifications

- Do not use AI that infers 3D from images (such as TripoSR).
- Observe the image and model each part directly using Blender Python.
- Do not modify the original image. Output only to a new folder. Do not overwrite existing completed versions.
- Copy the reference image to the output folder, recording its absolute path and SHA-256 hash.
- Prioritize this specification document for modeling details; use the image only for fine-tuning.
- Record invisible parts such as the back and thickness as "assumptions".
- Do not record unexecuted items as "verified".

■ 3. Orientation and Overall Dimensions

Units are in meters.
Pommel at +Z, Sword tip at -Z. Front is -Y, Right is +X.
Sword tip z=0.00, Pommel top vertex z=1.20.

Total Length: 1.20
Max Width of Guard: 0.34
Max Width of Blade: 0.072
Outer Diameter of Grip: 0.04
Max Width of Pommel: 0.045

Z-axis Placement:
Sword Tip: 0.00
Base of Blade: 0.89
Center of Guard: 0.91
Start of Grip: 0.94
End of Grip: 1.13
Base of Pommel: 1.13
Top Vertex of Pommel: 1.20

*Note: These are design values, not actual physical measurements.*

■ 4. Parts (Divide into at least 10 types)

blade
A straight double-edged blade, tapering slightly towards the tip.
Length 0.89, Base width 0.072, Mid-width 0.056, Near-tip width 0.02
Thickness: Base 0.012, Mid 0.008, Near-tip 0.003
Cross-section: Hybrid diamond/lens shape. Center is thick, edges are thin, appearing sharpened.

guard_center
Gold color. Downward V-shape extending to the base of the blade.
Width 0.085, Height 0.09, Depth 0.022
Incorporate a diamond-shaped blue gem in the center. Surround with beveled decorative frame.

guard_arm_left / guard_arm_right
Curved arms. Extending outward, slightly downward.
Length 0.127, Thickness 0.018, Depth 0.016, Tip drop 0.015
Slightly widen towards the tip, ending with a beveled cap. Right arm can be a mirror of the left.

gem_frame
Diamond-shaped gold frame. Height 0.05, Width 0.03, Depth 0.012
Slightly raised above surrounding surfaces.

gem_blue
Beveled diamond gemstone. Height 0.028, Width 0.016, Depth 0.008
Must appear clearly blue at normal viewing distance.

grip_core
Cylinder to loose octagon. Length 0.19, Diameter 0.034
Surface is dark brown leather. Silhouette is straight, passing through the center.

leather_wrap
Intersecting braid or spiral band. Band width 0.006, Relief 0.002
Diagonal intersections must be visible from the front.

pommel_collar
Short gold ring between grip and pommel. Height 0.018, Diameter 0.03

pommel
Beveled cone shape. Height 0.055, Max width 0.045, Base width 0.022
Tip ends with a pointed face. Should look like metal or pale crystalline metal.

■ 5. Materials (Colors are RGB, 0-1)

blade_steel  Color 0.72 / 0.74 / 0.77  Metallic 1.0  Roughness 0.28  (Brush finish, not overly polished)
guard_gold   Color 0.74 / 0.62 / 0.30  Metallic 1.0  Roughness 0.24  (Warm fantasy gold)
gem_blue     Color 0.16 / 0.33 / 0.70  Metallic 0.0  Roughness 0.08  (Opaque gem without transmission is acceptable)
leather_dark Color 0.22 / 0.14 / 0.10  Metallic 0.0  Roughness 0.72  (Dark brown leather)
leather_wrap Color 0.18 / 0.11 / 0.08  Metallic 0.0  Roughness 0.76  (Slightly darker than core)
pommel_metal Color 0.66 / 0.63 / 0.58  Metallic 1.0  Roughness 0.30  (Brighter metal)

■ 6. Modeling Rules

- Prioritize silhouette over detail.
- Do not turn image highlights/shadows directly into geometry.
- Blade edges must be distinctly thinner than the center.
- Guard should not be flat; show layering.
- Back view can reuse front construction (due to lack of reference).
- Name parts descriptively and keep them editable.
- Triangulate n-gons only immediately before GLB export.

■ 7. UV and Texture

- Create UVs for all meshes, avoiding overlaps.
- Combine into a single 2048x2048 atlas.
- Bake Base Color, Roughness, Metallic, and Normal maps.
- Embed textures within the GLB; do not rely on external files.

■ 8. Quality Guidelines

Target triangle count: 15,000–45,000.
This is a guideline; do not add geometry solely to meet the lower limit.
Usage: Static game assets and multi-angle sprites.

■ 9. Execution Order

1. Create a new output folder. Do not overwrite existing completed versions.
2. Copy the reference image to the output destination.
3. Recalculate SHA-256, recording match and local absolute path.
4. Implement modeling script according to specifications.
5. Run Blender in background mode to create editable source and preview.
6. Review preview, prioritizing corrections to silhouette and connections.
7. Perform UV unwrapping and PBR baking.
8. Export GLB.
9. Reload into an empty scene for verification.
10. Update records with measured values and actual verification results.

Notes:
- Do not include excessive detail from the start.
- Prioritize ratios of blade, guard, hilt, gem, and pommel.
- Since only one front view exists, design thickness and back conservatively.
- If dimensions or shapes change, briefly record changes and reasons.
- Do not proceed to final baking or video production until shape is finalized.
- Record unexecuted or failed items as-is.

■ 10. Acceptance Criteria

- Overall silhouette closely matches the reference image.
- Proportions, guard spread, hilt thickness, and gem position are correct.
- Does not look flat when viewed diagonally.
- No unintended gaps, intersections, or black holes between parts.
- Metal, leather, and gem materials are distinguishable.
- Shape, UV, normals, tangents, and textures are preserved after reloading GLB.

■ 11. Mandatory Checks Before Export

- GLB header and data length are correct.
- All faces have Position, Normal, UV, and Tangent data.
- Contains Base Color, Metallic/Roughness, and Normal maps.
- Images are embedded within the GLB.
- No abnormal coordinate values.
- No isolated vertices or edges.
- Record part count, triangle count, and size.
- Visually inspect reloaded GLB from front, diagonal, back, and detail views.

Do not mark failures as complete. Distinguish and record unexecuted, failed, and passed states.

entries.title: Building D&D Terrain with GPT-6 Astra
entries.description: Showcase of using GPT-6 Astra to assemble 3D printed terrain pieces for Dungeons & Dragons. The workflow involves generating geometry, segmenting parts, and using Astra via Blender MCP to arrange floors and cut printable STLs.
entries.prompt:
Building terrain for a massive D&D table with AI.

First test house printed and assembled.

It starts with AI generation. I generated the house geometry, then ran a segment model on it to get the separate parts.

The whole set of parts went to GPT-6 Astra, and it assembled them into floors. Ground floor, upper floor, roof, each one a piece that lifts off the stack.

After that, mirroring the outside in. The generated house has windows and doors only on the outer surface, so from the inside the walls are flat. I want these buildings playable on the inside, which means those openings have to be there as well. In Blender MCP, Astra mirrored that geometry inward, added a simple vertical ladder between the floors and steps in front of the door, then cut everything into printable parts and exported the STLs.

Then I printed it and put it together as a test. It looks good and it's fun to handle, the whole thing opens up the way I wanted. The seams are the weak part: flat cuts running straight across the model, right through bare wall surfaces, hard to hide.

On the next buildings the cuts should follow the model structure instead of ignoring it. Put them where the geometry already breaks: windows, door frames. Add sockets on the mating faces so the parts line up on their own.

Gluing and painting are still ahead. This one was a test of the whole pipeline and I'm happy with where it landed. I know what to fix now, and the next models should be easier to assemble.

you hand the model a data model instead of a vibe

preload all 4 images so nothing flickers

the layout stays identical between states, only the color moves

now the model has a schema to follow, so it only changes the one thing you told it to

entries.title: D&D Table Production Workflow
entries.description: A step-by-step guide on using GPT-6 Astra to block out a D&D campaign table town, followed by 3D asset generation and preparation for printing.
entries.prompt:
Astra blocked out the whole town in primitives first. Boxes standing in for houses, roads, open squares. We also made a small mood reference so we both knew what the town should feel like. Everything is cheap to move around while it's still a box.

Buildings I generate in 3DAIStudio. Image reference for each house first, then the 3D model from it. Getting the picture first matters: a house I don't like dies in seconds instead of after the model is done. I kept switching generators inside it, some houses came out better in Tripo 3.1, some in Hi3D 3.0, it's all in one box there. It also plugs into your agent over MCP. And Mesh 7.1 is landing there soon, promising 4k resolution, will see.

We drop the finished models back into the blockout and keep filling until it reads like a town instead of a pile of props. Street widths, where the open space goes, what's tall, what's low.

Now the part I'm starting today: cutting every house into floors. Ground floor, upper floor, roof, stacked so they lift off. Roof comes off, you play the top floor. A house that doesn't open is scenery, and I want the party to go inside. The generator only gives me the outside, so every floor gets a floor plate, walls with printable thickness, doorways wide enough for a base, stairs where they make sense.

entries.title: French Village 3D Scene Prompt
entries.description: A highly detailed prompt for generating a French village beside a lake in Blender via Codex/Astra. Specifies layout constraints (circular square in square village), visual style (warm stone, timber), and camera views.
entries.prompt:
I asked GPT-6 Astra Ultra for a small French village beside a lake, with one very specific detail: a circular central square inside a roughly square village.

Around ten houses, narrow flower-filled lanes, a fountain in the middle, and a path coming through the forest, crossing the village, and continuing down to the water. I wanted that feeling of discovering a quiet little place somewhere in the French countryside.

Along the shoreline, the idea was to have several fishing cabins, small wooden boats, and pockets of reeds. The forest frames the village, while the lake gives it an open side. Walking through the scene should gradually reveal those different spaces, from the enclosed woodland path to the village square and then the waterfront.

For this test, I’m using my custom workflow with Codex and Blender. It expands the initial description into a detailed production prompt, defines the layout, separates the important assets from reusable elements, and guides the scene through modeling, composition, rendering, and visual inspection.

The circular square is an interesting constraint because it affects everything around it. The houses need to frame it naturally while keeping the overall village compact and roughly square. The lanes need to connect the entrances, the fountain needs room around it, and the route toward the lake should remain easy to follow.

For the visual direction, the prompt calls for warm stone, aged plaster, timber details, tiled roofs, painted shutters, climbing plants, and flowers along the walls. The houses should share the same architectural character while having enough variation in height, roof shape, façades, and gardens to feel individually inhabited.

The workflow also asks for views from above, inside the square, along the lanes, at the fishing cabins, and looking back toward the village from the lake. Those different viewpoints are there to catch awkward spacing, hidden intersections, repetitive assets, and details that only work from one camera.

What interests me most with this scene is how much the atmosphere depends on those relationships. A glimpse of water between two houses, a flower-covered corner, or a narrow lane opening onto the fountain can give you a reason to keep walking.

That’s the feeling I want here: a small place you’d happily spend time wandering around.

entries.title: GTA 6 Beach House MCP Workflow
entries.description: Detailed prompt/workflow for building a complex 3D house in Blender/UEFN using concept art references and MCP tools.
entries.prompt:
GPT-6 made GTA 6 beach house using MCP tools!

Running Astra only through Blender MCP didn’t work for me, since it was mainly using primitive shapes to build the assets.

Now, with @Atlas3DAI workflows and Tripo, that changed!

Initially, I thought Tripo P2 would be the way to go: low-poly results straight into Blender. I tried it, but I didn’t get the results I wanted. Don’t get me wrong, P2 is great and a big improvement over P1, I just wanted more detail for this project. So I ended up using Tripo 3.1.

First, I needed a good starting point. I gave Astra some concept art and YouTube links, and it generated great reference images to work with.

With Atlas workflows, I used those references to generate images for all the individual parts. Using Atlas MCP, I exported them and automatically renamed everything based on the prompts. The next step was feeding the images into Atlas Batch Composer so it could run all the 3D generations in one go.

I asked Astra to optimize the generated assets to either 5K or 1K triangles, depending on their form and size. After a few tests, Astra made the process faster and faster. I gave it all 70 high-poly assets and let it run.

Astra then took care of the whole build. It imported the optimized assets into Blender and used the reference images to start recreating the house. I only had to give it directional feedback twice and manually rescale a few things.

There were still a lot of parts, though. Each beam was a separate object, and I knew that wasn’t ideal if I wanted to export the house to UEFN or Unreal Engine.

So I asked Astra to export only the unique assets. Then, using UEFN MCP, it rebuilt everything 1:1 while reusing modular parts like beams and windows.

I really enjoyed watching it place all the pieces in UEFN, almost like watching a timelapse of the house being built!

- Style: Simple expression reminiscent of N64-era games.

entries.title: GPT-6 Astra Gear Mechanism Simulation Prompt
entries.description: A prompt for GPT-6 Astra to build a browser-based 3D simulation of a gear train with correct physical meshing and ratios.
entries.prompt:
Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra had to build a machine where a 60-tooth gear driving a 20-tooth gear turns it exactly three times faster.

In a real mechanism, every gear has to mesh with its neighbor. The teeth need the same size and spacing or they won't fit together, and the speed of each gear comes straight from its tooth count. A gear with 60 teeth driving one with 20 turns it three times faster, no exceptions.

That's why it's hard to simulate. You can't spin a few circles and call it clockwork. If the ratios are wrong, teeth pass through each other. If the alignment is off, the gears jam or drift apart, and every mistake shows the moment it starts turning.

That's also what makes it a worthy test. Plenty of open builds hide sloppy logic behind nice visuals, and a gear train can't. The look of the mechanism is a free choice, but the meshing either works or it doesn't.

The prompt asked for a train of gears driven by a single source, every gear meshing with its neighbors at the correct ratio, teeth aligned, and at least three visible outputs turning at different speeds. Both models got one attempt, no style direction, and no chance to fix anything afterward.

You judge which one built the better mechanism.

entries.title: Interactive Solar System Simulation
entries.description: A prompt description for building a full 3D solar system with real astronomical data, orbital physics, camera controls, and planet information panels using GPT-6 Astra.
entries.prompt:
I ASKED GPT-6 ASTRA TO BUILD ME THE SOLAR SYSTEM. NOT A PICTURE OF IT — THE WHOLE THING, IN 3D, THAT I CAN FLY THROUGH.

Watch the clip. Every planet is real — real size, real color, real orbital speed. Mercury whipping around the Sun while Neptune barely crawls. Saturn's rings. Jupiter's storms. The asteroid belt. All of it moving exactly like the real thing.

I can grab the camera and fly from a view of the entire system down to the surface of Mars. Click any planet and it tells me everything — how long its day is, how much you'd weigh there, how hot it gets, how many moons it has.

There's a time slider. Push it and you watch years pass, planets racing around the Sun in seconds. It's hypnotic.

I didn't write a line of Three.js. I didn't model a single planet. I described what I wanted in plain English and Astra pulled the real astronomical data, built the physics, and rendered a working universe.

A planetarium spends millions on exhibits like this. I made it in an afternoon with a sentence.

We went from "AI writes text" to "AI builds you a universe" faster than anyone was ready for.

Where would you fly first?

entries.title: FOE TO FLEET Browser Shooter Game
entries.description: A prompt for developing a bullet-hell shooting game where defeated enemies join the player's fleet as weapons or shields, built with GPT-6 Astra.
entries.prompt:
【GPT-6 Astra】倒した敵が仲間になるシューティングゲームを開発【FOE TO FLEET】

【作業内容】
GPT-6 Astraを使用し、倒した敵が仲間になる弾幕シューティングゲーム「FOE TO FLEET」のMVPを開発・公開しました！
約2分でクリア可能な短時間型ゲームです。
仲間は敵を撃つ「武器」にも、敵弾を受け止める「盾」にもなります。
敵の時の能力（武器と最大HP）が引き継がれるため、強敵を倒すほど艦隊が強化されます。

【結果・所感】
敵を仲間に変え、武器や盾として活用しながら、弾幕を乗り切るシステムは斬新でとても面白いと感じます。
今後、ボスの実装やUI/UXの洗練などの肉付けを施せばより面白くなるかもしれません。

【使用技術】
・Codex (gpt-6-astra): メイン機能の設計・実装、サブ機能の設計
・Codex (gpt-5-luna): サブ機能の実装
・React / TypeScript / Vite: アプリ実装・開発サーバー
・Canvas 2D / Web Audio API: 描画・効果音
・Tailwind CSS: UI
・Playwright: 自動テスト
・game-ui-designスキル、game-ui-uxスキル: UI/UXの洗練

【動画タイムライン】
0:00 プレイ開始
0:53 ゲームクリア
0:54 タイトルと設定画面

【本ゲームのURL】
リプライからご確認ください。

【今後の展望】
1. ボスの実装
2. 仲間の加入方式の拡張
現状は仲間が満員時（最大12機）は仲間が加入されません。仲間が撃退され欠員発生後、新たに倒した敵が加入される方式となっています。
これを修正し、満員時に倒したより強い敵と既存の仲間を入れ替える、あるいは満員時に倒した敵をストックし欠員が出た場合にストックから即座に補充する方式に変更することを試します。

3. UI/UXの洗練
エフェクト・HUD・サウンド・アニメーションなどを追加・修正し、プレイヤーがより心地よい体験ができることを目指します。

4. ステージの追加

中式重檐寺庙、翘角琉璃瓦、青绿色屋顶、金色屋脊、朱红立柱、格栅门窗、山门、钟亭、香炉、石灯、石板庭院、松树、粉色花树与荷花池。

entries.title: Explorable Medieval Castle with Mechanical Physics
entries.description: A detailed 3D creation prompt for a large, interactive medieval fortress featuring explorable interiors, prison cells, and working drawbridge mechanics.
entries.prompt: build a medieval castle I could explore from the prison cells to the top of the keep, with a drawbridge that actually controls whether I can get inside. a large fortress surrounded by water-filled moats, an imposing gatehouse, several towers, thick defensive walls and a central keep rising above everything else. You approach on foot, cross the wooden drawbridge, pass beneath the portcullis and enter a large courtyard that connects the different parts of the castle. rooms with a clear purpose: a banquet hall with long tables and a large fireplace, a kitchen with adjoining food storage, guardrooms, an armory, bedrooms and living quarters. Below ground, a darker prison contains individual cells, iron bars, chains and doors you can open. Staircases lead up through the towers and onto the battlements, where you can walk around the perimeter and look down over the courtyard and moat. The exterior needs to look convincing, but every room also has to fit inside its building. Floors need to align with doorways, spiral staircases need enough headroom, and tower entrances need to connect to the wall walks at the correct height. start with the layout, floor plans and connections between spaces before detailed modeling. It establishes the visual references, builds the architectural components, furnishes each area, then checks the scene from above, inside the rooms and at player height. repeated render, inspect and refine passes, with reference comparisons to catch problems in proportions, materials and composition. The drawbridge gets its own mechanical requirements: a real hinge, attached chains, visible operating machinery and collision that follows the deck as it moves. The portcullis operates independently, and both mechanisms need to handle obstructions without trapping the player inside the geometry. enter through the gate, wander into the kitchen, find the stairs down to the prison, then climb all the way back up to a tower lookout through one continuous, coherent place.
