entries.title: GTA-Inspired 3D Car Chase Pipeline
entries.description: A comprehensive prompt workflow for GPT-6 Astra and Blender to create a cartoon-style vehicle pursuit, covering character design, animation rigs, and final rendering with PixVerse.
entries.prompt: Create an original {argument name="style" default="GTA-inspired cartoon car chase"} using this workflow: Design: Define one main driver, one getaway car, one pursuing car, and one {argument name="environment" default="urban environment"}. Keep their designs consistent. Plan three 4-second shots: rear tracking pursuit, side tracking through a sharp turn, and a wide exit shot. Build in Blender: Create clean gray models and functional character and vehicle rigs. No textures or UV unwrapping are required. Animate and test: Animate the driver, steering, wheel rotation, vehicles, and cameras. Maintain coherent travel direction and vehicle order. Fix clipping, floating wheels, sliding tires, broken poses, and hands losing contact with the steering wheel. Render in Blender: Render frames 1–288 at 1280×720, 24 fps. Assemble actual Blender-rendered frames into a complete 12-second gray-model master. Export each shot separately and render matching gray stills as shape and composition references. Finish with PixVerse Plugin: Use Seedance 2.5 at 720p, processing each shot separately. Use the Blender clips as motion references and the gray stills as shape references. Define a consistent cartoon color palette in the generation prompt. Preserve camera movement, action timing, character and vehicle designs, and vehicle count. Review and deliver: Inspect both complete videos for visual defects and continuity. Repair Blender issues and regenerate only failed Seedance shots, with at most two retries per shot. Deliver the editable .blend, the native 720p Blender gray-model video, the separately labeled 720p Seedance version, and a brief assessment of remaining limitations.

entries.title: Cinematic Wizard Workshop 3D Workflow
entries.description: A deep dive prompt for creating a 3D wizard's workshop in Blender, focusing on first-person animation and realistic lighting transitions.
entries.prompt: Create a 12-second, single-take white-model animation in Blender based on the attached reference image, then use PixVerse with Seedance 2.5 to transform the exported animation into a cinematic, {argument name="style" default="Witcher-3-inspired"} {argument name="scene" default="wizard workshop"} sequence. In Blender, use the reference image to guide the room layout, architecture, furniture, and props. Build an editable low-poly scene with clean meshes and UVs, using simple white or light-gray materials. Include stone walls, wooden shelves, an arched window, a fireplace, books, an astronomical instrument, and an alchemy table filled with potion bottles. Keep the silhouettes readable and the room proportions believable. Animate a low first-person viewpoint with exactly one right hand holding one {argument name="item" default="potion"}. Begin with the bottle resting near the lower-right edge while the character looks around the workshop and toward the window. Raise the potion naturally, pause to examine it, shift focus onto the bottle, then lower it while turning toward the fireplace and glowing reagents. Leave a small gap between the palm and bottle while maintaining believable fingertip contact. Use smooth changes in speed, gentle curved head movements, subtle breathing, and slight arm lag. Check the complete action at normal playback for clipping, awkward grip, abrupt turns, and excessive shaking. Keep the Blender fireplace simple: use logs, low embers, and flickering light. Avoid solid cones or flame-shaped meshes, which can be interpreted as glowing rocks. Prepare a separate fireplace detail from the reference image to guide the final appearance. Export the complete white-model MP4. Then generate a 12-second video with PixVerse, explicitly referencing the Blender-exported white-model video as the camera, action, and spatial reference, the attached image as the scene appearance reference, and the fireplace detail as the fire reference. Preserve the continuous shot, low viewpoint, single-hand potion action, room layout, and timing. Enrich the scene with weathered stone, carved wood, worn leather, iron fittings, and realistic glass. Combine cool window light and drifting dust with warm fireplace illumination and softly glowing magical liquids. Create natural wood fire with thin, irregular flames curling between charred logs, glowing embers, occasional sparks, and subtle smoke. Keep the hand anatomy, bottle shape, fire movement, and focus transitions consistent throughout. Review the full generated video, especially the hand action and fireplace. Deliver the white-model MP4, the PixVerse-rendered MP4, and the editable Blender project. After acceptance, retain the latest approved versions and move older versions to recoverable storage.

entries.title: GTA-Style 3D Car Chase Workflow
entries.description: A comprehensive multi-stage prompt for GPT-6 Astra and Blender to design and animate a 3D car chase scene, followed by final rendering polish using the PixVerse plugin.
entries.prompt:
以下の制作工程に沿って、オリジナルのGTA風3Dカーチェイスを制作してください。

【デザイン】
メインのドライバー1人、逃走車1台、追跡車1台、都市の舞台1つを設定し、それぞれのデザインを一貫させてください。各4秒、合計3つのショットを計画してください。
・後方から車両を追う追跡ショット
・急カーブを曲がる車両を側面から追うショット
・車両が走り去る様子を広く捉えるショット

【Blenderで構築】
整ったグレーモデルと、動作可能なキャラクター・車両のリグを作成してください。テクスチャやUV展開は不要です。

【アニメーションとテスト】
ドライバー、ハンドル操作、車輪の回転、車両、カメラをアニメーション化してください。進行方向と車両の前後関係を一貫させ、めり込み、車輪の浮き、タイヤの不自然な滑り、ポーズの崩れ、手がハンドルから離れる問題を修正してください。

【Blenderでレンダリング】
フレーム1〜288を1280×720、24fpsでレンダリングしてください。実際にBlenderでレンダリングしたフレームをつなぎ、12秒のグレーモデル版マスター動画を作成してください。各ショットを個別に書き出し、形状と構図の参照用に、対応するグレーの静止画もレンダリングしてください。

【PixVerseプラグインで仕上げ】
Seedance 2.5を720pで使用し、各ショットを個別に処理してください。Blenderの動画を動きの参照に、グレーの静止画を形状の参照に使用してください。生成プロンプトで映像全体に統一感のある配色を指定してください。カメラの動き、アクションのタイミング、キャラクターと車両のデザイン、車両数を維持してください。

【確認と納品】
完成した両方の動画を確認し、映像の不具合やショット間のつながりを点検してください。Blender側の問題を修正し、Seedanceで失敗したショットのみを再生成してください。再試行は各ショット最大2回までとします。

編集可能な.blendファイル、ネイティブ720pのBlenderグレーモデル動画、Seedance版と明記した720p動画、残っている制約についての簡潔な評価を納品してください。
entries.translated_prompt:
Please create an original GTA-style 3D car chase following the production process below.

[Design]
Set up one main driver, one getaway car, one pursuit car, and one city setting, keeping the designs consistent. Plan three shots of 4 seconds each, for a total of 12 seconds:
- A pursuit shot following the vehicle from behind.
- A side-view shot following the vehicle as it takes a sharp turn.
- A wide shot capturing the vehicle as it drives away.

[Build in Blender]
Create a clean gray model and functional rigs for the characters and vehicles. Textures and UV unwrapping are not required.

[Animation and Testing]
Animate the driver, steering wheel operation, wheel rotation, vehicles, and camera. Maintain consistency in the direction of travel and vehicle positioning, and fix issues such as clipping, floating wheels, unnatural tire sliding, pose breakdown, and hands coming off the steering wheel.

[Render in Blender]
Render frames 1 to 288 at 1280x720, 24fps. Concatenate the frames rendered in Blender to create a 12-second gray model master video. Export each shot individually and render corresponding gray still images for shape and composition reference.

[Finishing with PixVerse Plugin]
Use Seedance 2.5 at 720p and process each shot individually. Use the Blender video as a motion reference and the gray still images as shape references. Specify a consistent color scheme for the entire video in the generation prompt. Maintain camera movement, action timing, character and vehicle designs, and the number of vehicles.

[Review and Delivery]
Review both completed videos, checking for visual artifacts and the continuity between shots. Correct issues on the Blender side and regenerate only the shots that failed in Seedance. Allow a maximum of 2 retries per shot.

Deliver an editable .blend file, the native 720p Blender gray model video, the 720p video clearly labeled as the Seedance version, and a concise evaluation of any remaining constraints.

entries.title: High-Speed Shuttle Chase 3D Scene
entries.description: A detailed prompt for creating a high-speed shuttle flight sequence in Blender, featuring a city canyon, barrel rolls, and motion blur for a sense of extreme speed.
entries.prompt: Create a 10-second, single-take white-model shuttle flight in Blender. Build an original shuttle and a dense city canyon stretching several kilometers. Animate extremely fast forward flight along an extended route, covering over two kilometers without slowing down. Weave through narrow gaps and under bridges, change altitude, and perform two smooth barrel rolls in opposite directions. Make the speed unmistakable: nearby buildings streak backward, bridges whip overhead, and foreground structures rapidly sweep past the frame edges. Use strong directional motion blur on the environment while keeping the shuttle readable. Dense obstacles, close passes, and strong foreground-to-background parallax should convey sustained, full-throttle flight. Use a smooth wide-angle chase camera close behind and slightly above the shuttle, racing forward at matching speed. Keep the nose pointing into the city and the engines facing the camera. No cuts, camera shake, camera barrel rolls, slow motion, or deceleration at the ending. Test clearance, motion continuity, and the sense of speed at normal playback. Use PixVerse to render the final white-model animation from Blender references, preserving the extreme speed, flight path, and camera movement. Deliver the final MP4, editable Blender project, and brief notes on limitations.

entries.title: Photorealistic Japanese Torii Shrine Scene
entries.description: A comprehensive 3D creation workflow for Blender and PixVerse to build a cinematic Japanese torii shrine with animated foliage and birds.
entries.prompt: Create an original Japanese torii shrine scene using PixVerse and Blender. Complete these steps: Create the concept: Use PixVerse to generate a photoreal reference image. Lock the torii design, materials, lighting, and environment for consistency. Build the 3D scene: Create an editable textured model in Blender. Clean the topology, unwrap the UVs, and add suitable animation controls. Add movement: Include foreground leaves that partially obscure the wide shots, gently moving foliage, and birds flying visibly across the scene. Animate the cameras: Create a 12-second sequence with three shots: an arcing approach, a lateral detail shot, and a rising pullback. Keep movement smooth and framing clear. Render in Blender: Export a native camera video and a separate neutral gray clay reference video using the same animation. Save them beside the Blender project. Generate the photoreal film: Use PixVerse Seedance with the gray video for camera and action reference and the unchanged photoreal image for appearance. Generate a 1080p, 16:9 video with only natural environmental sounds—wind, rustling leaves, and bird wings. No music or voices. Check and deliver: Review every shot for consistent design, photoreal textures, visible birds, smooth motion, and correct audio. Fix issues within the approved budget and document remaining limitations. Save the editable Blender project, videos, reference image, and a brief production assessment in the same folder. Key points: Never use the colored low-poly video as the Seedance reference. Check the entire film, especially the final wide shot.

entries.title: Advanced 3D Character Processing Pipeline
entries.description: A detailed set of requirements for Astra to refine textures, weights, shading, and engine export for a 3D character.
entries.prompt:
■テクスチャ/UVの細部調整
マルチビュー＆全身サイズ投影の関係もあるので、髪の色が肌メッシュの上に少し漏れている部分あり、これおを調整（🌙マークとかも少しブレはある）
■スケルトンとウェイトの調整
Tripo内にも自動スキニングはあるが、サイドポニーテールやスカートに揺れを入れたいのでAstraにやらせてみることに
あと、ケープがあるので補助骨とかも追加したいから
■シェーディング
アジア圏でみられるようなアニメ系シェーディングによるマテリアル表現
■フェイシャル
モーフによるFACS・リップシンク対応
目をまばたきできるようにする
■アニメ的な陰影
顔はアニメ的な陰影をつけたいのでSDFを使ったライティング表現ができるようにする
■UE/Unityへの繋ぎ
UE5.8上での検証も自動化
entries.translated_prompt:
■Texture/UV detail adjustment
Due to multi-view and full-body size projection, hair color has leaked onto the skin mesh in some parts. Adjust this (the 🌙 mark also has some blurring).
■Skeleton and weight adjustment
Although Tripo has automatic skinning, I want to add movement to the side ponytail and skirt, so I'll have Astra do it.
Also, there's a cape, so I want to add helper bones etc.
■Shading
Material expression using anime-style shading seen in the Asian region.
■Facial
FACS and lip-sync support via morphs. Make eyes blinkable.
■Anime-like shadows
I want the face to have anime-style shadows, so enable lighting expressions using SDF.
■Connection to UE/Unity
Automate verification on UE5.8.

entries.title: Minimalist Architectural House Design
entries.description: A foundational prompt for architectural visualization, initiating the creation of a minimalist house with a detailed garden using Blender and Unreal Engine 5.
entries.prompt: 设计一栋极简但细节丰富的房子，带漂亮花园。加入黄昏光线与森林环境。先出平面图供人审批：围绕庭院的 U 型单层方案，卧室不被穿越式动线占用、厨房工作区不被过道打断。几何级的细节：沙发坐垫带滚边、床有床架/排骨架/床垫/床品的完整分层、衣柜有内部和挂杆、水槽是真挖空的凹碗、餐桌上摆着餐具。靠垫和床品是手工塑形。材质混合自建着色与 Poly Haven 扫描贴图。光源与可见灯具对应、在灯罩里放入发光灯泡；桌上放面包、香草，茶几上摊开日记、老花镜、钥匙。1.65m 视高、24–26mm 镜头。Cycles 渲染 900 帧（自适应采样 + OpenImageDenoise）。Unreal Engine 5 可交互第一人称漫游：第一人称角色、碰撞、E 键交互（开门/抽屉、开关灯、操作咖啡机：按按钮、出咖啡、液面上升）。HELIOS（戴森球，5120 块面板）、AURELION-07 星舰（含程序化材质区分陶瓷装甲/机加工金属/玻璃）、莫奈吉维尼花园（睡莲池、绿桥）。
entries.translated_prompt: Design a minimalist but detail-rich house with a beautiful garden. Add dusk lighting and a forest environment. Provide a floor plan first for approval: a U-shaped single-story layout around a courtyard, ensuring bedrooms are not occupied by through-traffic and the kitchen workspace is not interrupted by corridors. Geometric-level details: sofa cushions with welts, beds with full layering of frame/slats/mattress/bedding, wardrobes with interiors and hanging rods, sinks as truly hollowed-out bowls, and tableware set on the dining table. Cushions and bedding are manually shaped. Materials mixed from custom shaders and Poly Haven scanned textures. Light sources correspond to visible fixtures, with glowing bulbs placed inside lampshades; bread and herbs on the table, and a diary, reading glasses, and keys spread out on the coffee table. 1.65m eye level, 24–26mm lens. Cycles rendering 900 frames (adaptive sampling + OpenImageDenoise). Unreal Engine 5 interactive first-person walkthrough: first-person character, collisions, E-key interaction (open doors/drawers, switch lights, operate coffee machine: press button, dispense coffee, rising liquid level). HELIOS (Dyson sphere, 5120 panels), AURELION-07 Starship (including procedural materials distinguishing ceramic armor/machined metal/glass), Monet's Giverny Garden (water lily pond, green bridge).

entries.title: Stylized Japanese Flower Shop Exploded View Animation
entries.description: A comprehensive prompt for creating a stylized Japanese flower shop in Blender, including detailed environmental props and a high-impact dynamic exploded-view animation sequence.
entries.prompt: Use Blender MCP to build a small, stylized {argument name="shop type" default="Japanese flower shop"} scene. Focus on faithfully recreating the key visual elements: the {argument name="awning color" default="green"} awnings, the rooftop sign displaying the Japanese text “花屋”, flower pots and plants arranged in front of the shop, the vending machine, bicycles, traffic light, utility poles, surrounding trees, and other recognizable street details. Render the scene in a {argument name="visual style" default="warm, charming cartoon style"}, with soft lighting, appealing materials, and a cozy atmosphere. Create a high-impact, dynamic exploded-view animation of the entire flower shop scene. The explosion should be bold and exaggerated rather than subtle. Smoothly and systematically separate the individual components outward to dramatically reveal the construction and interior of the flower shop. During the explosion, have the exterior walls, surrounding trees, utility poles, signs, awnings, bicycles, flower pots, plants, street props, and other environmental elements fly outward or backward, creating enough open space for the viewer to clearly see inside the flower shop. Break the building into meaningful structural layers so that the interior architecture, furniture, decorations, flowers, plants, shelves, and smaller details become clearly visible. The vending machine should also explode into its individual components. Its exterior panels should separate, and the individual soda bottles and cans inside should dynamically fly outward, spreading into an organized formation so they remain clearly readable. Small components and details can travel farther to make the sequence more visually exciting. Use staggered timing, different movement speeds, rotation, depth, and layered trajectories to give the explosion a strong sense of energy and impact while keeping every component visually organized and easy to follow. Avoid having everything move outward at exactly the same time or speed. Once the entire scene is fully exploded, hold the composition briefly so the viewer can clearly observe the internal structure and all the separated components. Then reverse the sequence: the soda bottles, vending machine parts, plants, props, interior objects, walls, trees, utility poles, signs, bicycles, and all other components should fly smoothly back into place and reassemble into the complete flower shop scene. The entire animation should feel energetic, cinematic, satisfying, and visually impactful, with strong motion and clear transformation between the complete scene, the fully exploded state, and the final reassembled scene. Keep the motion layered, readable, and carefully choreographed throughout. Use a neutral studio background during the exploded-view sequence so that the separated objects and internal structures remain clearly visible. Final deliverables: A fully rendered animation and an editable Blender 3D project file. All objects, components, collections, materials, and major scene elements must be

entries.title: Interactive 3D SVG Logo Deformer
entries.description: A sophisticated agentic prompt for building a professional browser-based 3D instrument using Three.js and React. It includes detailed instructions for geometry, chrome materials, physics-based interactions, and an autonomous iteration loop with visual verification.
entries.prompt:
/goal Build Brand Instrument: a polished browser-based 3D creative instrument closely matching the attached reference image. Work autonomously through implementation, real-browser inspection, critique and fixes. Aim for a reviewable result within 3.5 hours, with a requested upper time budget of 4 hours. Record start time and check elapsed time between iterations. Finish earlier if the acceptance criteria are met.

FIRST
Inspect the reference and read project instructions. Verify that you can launch the app, interact with its browser and inspect actual screenshots. Save the available reference in the project for repeated comparison. If the reference or browser inspection is unavailable, report that immediately. Never invent visual verification.

SCOPE
One excellent M sculpture, chrome material and refined interaction.
Use TypeScript, React, Vite and Three.js. Prefer WebGPURenderer with TSL and tested WebGL2 fallback. Adapt implementation where necessary while preserving real 3D. Separate geometry, motion, rendering and UI. No model API is needed at runtime.

VISUAL TARGET
Preserve the reference's flowing M, dense parallel silver plates, substantial volume, clean bevels, narrow gaps, broad white studio reflections, dark reflected bands, soft grounding shadow, white background and restrained black Manrope typography. The sculpture dominates the viewport.
Improve physical coherence and usability without redesigning the art direction. The reference is an artistic target, never a texture used to fake the product.

GEOMETRY AND MOTION
Build volumetric plates with sufficient topology for local bending, driven by a controllable rig or guide curves. Dragging the right arm creates a smooth local fan/wave with anchored regions and coherent influence across neighboring plates.
Release restores the rest configuration with stable, frame-rate-independent damped dynamics. Preserve believable thickness and limit extreme deformation. Keep normals, shadows and pointer picking consistent with the deformed surface.
No screen-space displacement, flat-image warping, prerecorded hero video or screenshot stand-in.

FUNCTIONS
Working drag/release, camera orbit to inspect depth, spread adjustment, stiffness/damping controls, Reset and PNG export.
Prioritize this core. Arbitrary SVG import, audio and extra modes are later work. Show only functional controls.

ITERATION LOOP
Implement a valuable change.
Run the app and inspect real screenshots at consistent viewport/camera settings.
Exercise drag, release, reset and export.
Identify the three largest remaining visual or functional defects.
Fix the most important defect and repeat.
Save useful checkpoints and comparison images. Preserve the best working version. If repeated changes fail, change the approach.
A successful build alone does not mean completion.

ACCEPTANCE
Recognizable sculptural M; crisp separated plates; convincing chrome; close reference composition.
S

entries.prompt:
First search for the "/unlazy" skill, read it fully, and use it throughout the entire task.

Treat this as a major visual build lasting at least {argument name="minimum duration" default="5 hours"}. Prefer {argument name="optimal duration" default="8–24 hours"} of meaningful implementation and iteration if the environment allows it. Do not stop after producing one decent-looking scene.

Create an extremely detailed real-time {argument name="subject" default="3D forest"} in the browser. Nothing else. No landing page, cards, story, marketing UI, dashboard, or unnecessary text. The forest itself is the entire experience.

Push density and visual quality extremely hard.

Build massive amounts of detailed grass, varied trees, branches, leaves, bushes, ferns, moss, flowers, weeds, roots, fallen wood, stones, soil, leaf litter, small plants, terrain variation, and tiny environmental details.

The forest should feel almost excessively dense. Empty ground should be rare.

Focus obsessively on:
realistic tree silhouettes,
dense grass,
natural asset variation,
rich colors,
lighting,
contact shadows,
wind,
foliage motion,
atmospheric depth,
fog,
sun shafts,
particles,
terrain,
materials,
scale,
composition,
and detail at both close and far distances.

Avoid obvious repeating assets, billboard-looking foliage, tiled terrain, floating plants, plastic materials, identical trees, sparse procedural placement, excessive bloom, or a generic Three.js demo appearance.

Include smooth free-camera exploration.

Fix these issues and continue increasing quality throughout the run.

The goal is not feature count. The goal is to make one browser forest look completely ridiculous in terms of detail and atmosphere.

entries.title: Three.js Solar System Video
entries.description: Details on creating a solar system tour video with Three.js and GPT-6.2 Astra, including technical constraints.
entries.prompt:
GPT6.2-Astra × Three.jsの検証。

太陽系周遊動画のブラッシュアップ版です。
各惑星の中まで侵入するシーンを追加、ついでに惑星の特徴も添えて。

質感に関しては、NASAの観測データを取得させて、テクスチャのクオリティを向上しました。

以下は、Astraのコメント全文です。

「特に苦労したのは、飛行速度を保ったままカメラのガタつきを取ることです。 山越えで高度と視線が急変していたため、少し先の稜線を読んで手前から上昇する航路に変更。全19,260フレームを測定すると、カメラの角加速度の最大値は約81%下がりました。もう一つの難所は水星です。低空のクレーターと全球地図をつなぐと地平線の地形が筋状に伸びたため、遠景まで地形を広げ、探査機の標高データへ滑らかに切り替えました。

主な技術は、Three.js/WebGL 2とGLSLです。NASAの夜間光データで地球の都市を光らせ、火星・水星では実測標高から凹凸の陰影を生成。海陸別の反射、独立して流れる雲、フレネル効果による大気の縁光、HDRブルームを重ね、FFmpegで映像化しました。」

---

修正は計4回、計2時間40分。

GPT6.2-Astra(ウルトラ、速度1.5倍)で、トークン消費は、大体15%でした。
entries.translated_prompt:
Verification of GPT6.2-Astra × Three.js.

This is a brushed-up version of the solar system tour video.
Added scenes where we penetrate into each planet, and also added features of the planets along with it.

Regarding texture quality, I had it fetch NASA observation data to improve the texture quality.

Below is the full comment from Astra.

"What was particularly difficult was removing camera jitter while maintaining flight speed. Because altitude and line of sight changed abruptly when crossing mountains, I changed the route to ascend from before reading the ridge line slightly ahead. When measuring all 19,260 frames, the maximum angular acceleration of the camera decreased by about 81%. Another difficult spot was Mercury. When connecting low-altitude craters with the global map, the horizon terrain stretched in streaks, so I expanded the terrain to the distance and smoothly switched to the probe's elevation data.

The main technologies are Three.js/WebGL 2 and GLSL. Using NASA's night light data to make Earth's cities glow, generating bump shadows from measured elevations on Mars and Mercury. Separate reflections for sea and land, independently flowing clouds, atmospheric rim lighting via Fresnel effect, overlaying HDR bloom, and rendering the video with FFmpeg."

---

Total 4 revisions, total time 2 hours 40 minutes.

With GPT6.2-Astra (Ultra, speed 1.5x), token consumption was roughly 15%.

entries.title: Mario Kart Style Racing Game Benchmark
entries.description: Benchmarking GPT-6 Astra Codex against Claude Code for creating a Mario Kart-style racing game with code only.
entries.prompt:
There are Three important points:
・Blender, Engine, and existing assets were not used; everything was created using "code only".
・For better or worse, this is about as far as you can get with a single prompt.
・Conversely, you can also look at it this way: you can get this far with just a single prompt.

Developer:
Backer | AAA programmer who has been active from the GBA era to the present.
Formerly CAPCOM Third Development Division (Console Game Development Department).

For the purpose of benchmarking artistic quality (integrated across programming, graphics, sound, and usability), I built a Mario Kart-style racing game using GPT Codex and Claude Code with a single prompt.
The person controlling this game is the account owner, Backer.
Although the gameplay video only shows a portion of the game, I built an entire stage without omitting any parts, from the title screen through the main loop to the end-condition check.

-----
■Left
-----
Claude Code Opus 5.5 | Amount of thinking:Ultracode
Claude Code Sonnet 5.5 | Amount of thinking:Ultracode

Point:
・Only the Claude Code was used.
・Claude work time: 6 hours 35 minutes
・API time included: 7 hours 20 minutes
・Backer himself did not write any code this time.
・Blender, MCP, Godot, Unity, Unreal Engine, etc. were not used.
・Professionals, amateurs, and beginners alike can all game operate and create game system content in the same way.

Rendering Style:
・Toon Shading

-----
■Center
-----
GPT-6 Astra Codex | Amount of thinking:Ultra

Point:
・Only the Codex was used.
・Codex work time: 68 minutes
・Backer himself did not write any code this time.
・Blender, MCP, Godot, Unity, Unreal Engine, etc. were not used.
・Professionals, amateurs, and beginners alike can all game operate and create game system content in the same way.

Rendering Style:
・Toon Shading (Simple)

-----
■Right
-----
GPT-6 Astra Codex | Amount of thinking:Extremely high

Point:
・Only the Codex was used.
・Codex work time: 47 minutes
・Backer himself did not write any code this time.
・Blender, MCP, Godot, Unity, Unreal Engine, etc. were not used.
・Professionals, amateurs, and beginners alike can all game operate and create game system content in the same way.

Rendering Style:
・Toon Shading (Simple)

-----
■Important
-----
On social media, you often see videos claiming that "AI created a complete Mario Kart with just one prompt," but that's a lie.
If it was truly created using only CodeAI (such as Codex or Claude Code) and no external tools, then it's only natural that it would "look like this," for better or for worse.
For a game to be polished, it's essential for the developers to fine-tune every element, including the program, system (game loop, game status management, character status management, state flag bits, event flag bits, proper variable definitions, structure/class management, pointers, pointer lists, functions, function lists, interrupt handling, hit detection, coordinate calculations, camera coordinates, lighting adjustments, shadow mapping, improving processing speed in real space, screen space, and projection space, etc.), modeling, shading, UI, sprites, creation and adjustment of various effects, presentation adjustments, coordinate movement, fading, alpha ring blending, sound production, and sound effect production.

-----
■Supplement
-----
On social media, you often see accounts trying to gain impressions or lying, posting things like, "The gaming industry is over! This was done with just one click and one line of prompts!" along with videos of existing, finished commercial games.
Frankly, these fake posts benefit no one and are not funny at all. Replies like, "This post isn't even funny as a joke," are common to these kinds of posts.
Instead of making such pointless posts that only waste viewers' time, it's far more worthwhile to look at the insights of people who bravely share the progress of their own games, even at the risk of their ideas being stolen, or, like Backer's posts, who complete a full stage and post it as an integrated benchmark (artistic benchmark).
At the very least, it's far better than looking at countless unfunny, fake posts that post things like, "The gaming industry is over! This was done with just one click and one line of prompts!" along with videos of existing, finished commercial games.

entries.title: Unreal Engine Hill Town Workflow with GPT-6 Astra
entries.description: A detailed workflow for building a playable hill town in Unreal Engine 5 using GPT-6 Astra to generate PCG tools and Blender for modeling. Includes specific prompts for converting OSM paths to splines and generating procedural generation rules.
entries.prompt:
Built a playable hill town in Unreal Engine 5 with GPT-6 Astra + Blender...

a Mont-Saint-Michel-style island town

the idea: Astra builds the PCG tools, then you edit a 2D map instead of prompting again. here's the workflow:

step 1: openstreetmap: export the real island's roads and paths as the base layout
step 2: gpt-6 astra: "convert these osm paths into splines and shape mesh terrain beneath them"
step 3: gpt-6 astra: write 5 pcg tools: roads, platforms, stairs, buildings, walls
step 4: unreal 5: stairs connect two surfaces and rebuild when you move either one. walls leave gaps wherever a route passes through
step 5: blender: model a small kit of facade, roof and wall modules, then export to unreal
step 6: gpt-6 astra: "turn this town into rules", then draw a vector map of a brand new one
step 7: unreal 5: the map's paths become editable splines, and the tools raise the town on their own
step 8: unreal 5: walk it at player scale. shift a walkway, lift a terrace, regenerate only that piece
step 9: unreal 5: detail pass with facade grammar, dormers, chimneys, shutters, vegetation, masonry

dragging a line on a map beats another prompt, another trip to blender and another wait.

entries.translated_prompt: I want to create a landing page for {argument name="topic" default="mountain homestay"}. Reference images are attached; follow their vibe.
